It’s Time to File Your FAFSA

The 2027–2028 FAFSA is now open! Every student should complete the FAFSA, regardless
                        of age, income, or family status to determine eligibility for financial aid. The earlier
                        you submit, the sooner KSU can process your information and send your award letter,
                        giving you more time to plan.
Learn More About FAFSA













Exploring academic options or planning your next semester?

Our course syllabi provide a transparent, detailed look into the learning experience
                                    so you can make informed decisions with confidence.Discover course content, expectations, and outcomes all in one place.
Browse Syllabi by Course









Why Choose KSU?



Awesome Location
Only 15 miles from the excitement of Atlanta, with even more excitement locally.
Over 190 Programs
A leader in innovative teaching and learning, KSU offers over 190 undergraduate, graduate
                                       and doctoral degrees and programs.
R2 University
Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2), placing
                                       it among an elite group of only 8 percent of U.S. colleges.






Fall 2027 Priority Deadline: Nov. 2The priority deadline for freshman and transfer freshman applications and document submissions for the Fall 2027 semester is November 2! Apply early and join The Nest! 







How much does it cost?

KSU is dedicated to ensuring that you know what to expect financially, and helping

Undergraduate Application

Professional Education

 





 
 
 
 

Undergraduate Application

 
 
 
 






Our number one priority at KSU is you and your success. We want your application process to be simple and exciting, no matter your application type. We’re excited that you’ve chosen KSU as your academic doorway to reach your future potential and purpose. 
We are here to help you during the entire application process. Welcome, future KSU
                           Owls!
apply
Visit Undergraduate Admissions






 
 
 
 

Graduate Application

 
 
 
 






KSU gives you the tools needed to advance in your career and find your path to success.
                           We support our graduates in returning to academia to become professionals that excel
                           in their field of interest. Our application process is straightforward and simple
                           to save you time and effort.
Get started on your graduate application today to start enhancing your skills as a KSU Owl. 
apply
Visit Graduate Admissions






 
 
 
 

Professional Education at KSU

 
 
 
 







It’s Your Profession. Soar Higher.

It’s time to start investing in yourself. Apply for a professional program at Kennesaw State to advance and skills to reach your professional and career goals faster.
Get ahead with professional certificates, corporate learning opportunities, community

Undergraduate Open House

Visitor Information







Welcome, Future KSU Owls!

Kennesaw State University is passionate about supporting you from the moment you step foot onto our campuses. We want you to see and experience what Owl Life is really like. With various ways to visit, our campus tours offer you a birds-eye view of all the places of interest you need to know about before you decide to join the Nest. 






 
 
 
 

There are Various Ways to Tour KSU

 
 
 
 






Visiting our campuses is a wonderful opportunity for future students, families and visitors to explore the KSU culture, experience the energy and learn about our Owl Nation. 
Both the Kennesaw and Marietta campuses are vibrant and teeming with spirit! Our tours
                           are designed to answer your questions and meet your needs so visiting Kennesaw State
                           is a breeze.











Experience KSU in Person





Schedule a Campus Tour
High School Group Tours













Experience KSU from Home





Kennesaw State Virtual Tour
Interactive Maps










 
 
 
 

Plan Your Visit

 
 
 
 








Our Campus programs and departments have exciting and interactive events that happen
                                 year-round. As you make your plans to visit Kennesaw State, please check out the following
                                 to make sure your visit goes smoothly. We hope you come to love KSU as much as we
                                 do.










Need Directions?

Kennesaw State University has two main campuses in Cobb County about 20-30 minutes north of Atlanta, GA, just off Interstate 75.

Parking & Campus Transportation Information

We welcome all visitors to Kennesaw State year-round for community events, tours and
                                    more. We provide convenient parking payments through the ParkMobile app for visitors
                                    at both campuses. Additionally, visit our Pay-per-Plate kiosks in each of our Visitor

Before you leave, make sure you check out our award-winning dining facilities and

We can’t wait to see you here!

Give to KSU




Kennesaw State University
Give








Ways to Give

Office of Development

KSU Foundation





Your gift to Kennesaw State University helps make a meaningful difference for generations
                        to come. You can be a part of advancing the university's goals by making a gift to
                        campus initiatives, specific programs, scholarships and/or colleges. Gift opportunities
                        are also available for cultural, athletic or educational outreach programs.





 
 
 
 

Donors at Kennesaw State are One of Our Greatest Assets

 
 
 
 






Our continued support from friends, faculty, staff, alumni, and parents has enabled KSU to reach a greater level of excellence and attract top-notch undergraduate and graduate students. Our university remains a leader in higher education thanks to the charitable gifts we receive from our generous donors. 
At KSU, donors truly make all the difference.






 
 
 
 

Ways to Give to KSU

 
 
 
 









There are many ways you can invest in Kennesaw State. We support your gifting through credit cards, checks, money orders and electronic funds transfers. You may also invest in KSU with a bequest or life income gift. 
Our staff is always happy to assist you in finding the type of gift that best meets
                                    your giving needs.
Give to KSU Online




We accept all gifts including: 




Online Giving
Mail
Recurring Credit/Debit Card Draft
Faculty / Staff Payroll Deduction
Matching Gifts






Stocks and Other Securities  
Gift Planning
Memorial Gifts
Gifts-in-Kind













 
 
 
 

Office of Development

 
 
 
 





Our Office of Development at Kennesaw State is dedicated to supporting our diverse giving communities and families. We meet you where you are and make your giving goals and dreams possible with various ways to give, friendly staff members to help direct your gifts and facilitate exciting donor features across the University. 






Where to Give



Friends & Family
Faculty & Staff
Scholarships
Gift Planning












Visit the Office of Development
See how your gift can be used for future KSU students








 
 
 
 

KSU Foundation

 
 
 
 









Our Kennesaw State University Foundation, Inc. is a nonprofit corporation that focuses on furthering the interests of KSU by supporting, guiding and protecting the university when receiving private gifts. 
We are committed to enhancing higher education for our faculty, staff and students and increasing the quality of life on our campuses. 














KSU Foundation

Meet the President's Cabinet

The President's Cabinet at Kennesaw State University is made up of bold, energetic leaders concerned with academic planning, administrative and university operations, communications, and student success. They collaborate to advance KSU's mission and vision and to increase student engagement, provide state-of-the-art student support, and keep a strong foundation for a positive impact on graduation and the college experience. 
Comprising a diverse assembly of visionary minds and seasoned professionals, the Cabinet
                     stands as the university's strategic compass, steering the institution towards academic
                     excellence, innovation, and growth. United by a shared commitment to elevate higher
                     education, this accomplished team seeks to help shape the university's path, uphold
                     its values, and nurture an environment of learning and progress.

Welcome to KSU’s Undergraduate Catalog!
The Kennesaw State University catalog contains important information and is the official source of the university’s academic programs, courses, and policies. The catalog should be used as a guide in conjunction with an academic advisor and DegreeWorks, in planning a course of study, and in meeting requirements for graduation. 
Click on the icons below to jump to helpful pages in our catalog and the Admissions and Financial Aid websites.












 
How the Catalog Works

If you’re looking for another publication (such as the Graduate Catalog, Student Handbook, Microcredentials Inventory, etc.) please use the drop-down menu in the top right corner of the catalog.
Advanced search features allow you to search for courses, policies, and degree programs using course prefix, course number, exact match or descriptive phrases.
Navigating to different sections of the catalog is easily done by clicking on the menu options on the left side of the screen.
Each section has a print-friendly view to allow for cleaner, more attractive pages when you print.
Help icons are readily available on each page.

If you’re not sure which catalog to use or have questions about choosing courses or degree programs, please reach out to an academic advisor at http://advising.kennesaw.edu/.




Southern Association of Colleges and Schools 
Kennesaw State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges to award baccalaureate, masters, specialist, and doctorate degrees. Kennesaw State University also may offer credentials such as certificates and diplomas at approved degree levels. Questions about the accreditation of Kennesaw State University may be directed in writing to the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges at 1866 Southern Lane, Decatur, GA 30033-4097, by calling (404) 679-4500, or by using information available on SACSCOC’s website (www.sacscoc.org).

Apply to KSU as a Transfer Student

We are glad you are considering transferring to the Owl Nation. As a transfer student, your smooth transition to Kennesaw State is our top priority. Whether you’re planning to complete your bachelor’s degree or are seeking a new college with greater opportunities, Kennesaw State provides the tools and support you need to transfer and succeed.
You should apply as a Transfer Student if you:

graduated from high school, and
earned 30 semester hours or 50 quarter hours of transferable college credit.

          Browse Professional Courses and Certificates
        






Artificial Intelligence (AI)


Learn applied AI skills in a variety of topics. 







Business and Management


Strengthen leadership, operations, and project management skills for today’s workplaces.







Computer-Aided Design (CAD)


Build AutoCAD 2D, 3D, and Revit skills for architecture, engineering, and design work.






Construction Fundamentals


Build practical, in-demand construction skills online, on your time.







Culinary Arts


Develop professional culinary, baking and pastry techniques for working in restaurants, catering, or working towards your personal goals.







Data Science & Analytics


Use data tools and techniques to turn raw information into insight.







Finance


Grow skills in bookkeeping and payroll.







Healthcare


Explore administrative certificates that support healthcare teams.







Marketing


Plan, create, and measure digital and social media campaigns that get results.







Patient Care


Prepare for hands-on roles working directly with patients in clinical settings.







Paralegal


Build foundational legal knowledge and skills..






Remote Drone Pilot Training


Develop the skills necessary to operate small unmanned aircraft system (sUAS) safely. 







Technology and Cybersecurity


Develop IT, networking, and cybersecurity skills for today’s digital workplace.


















          Why Choose KSU Community and Professional Education?
        

          From career certificates to English language programs, lifelong learning, and summer camps for teens — we offer something for every stage of life.
        




1

University-backed programs
Learn through Kennesaw State University — one of Georgia's largest public universities. Every program, from professional certificates to OLLI enrichment courses, carries the credibility of a KSU education.



2

Flexible formats for real life
Choose from in-person, hybrid, and online options built around your schedule — whether you're a working adult, an international student, or an adult learner with a full calendar.



3

Expert instructors
Our instructors bring real-world experience to every classroom and are practitionaers in their field.



4

Outcomes that matter
Professional certificates align to employer needs and industry credentials. IEP completers start a pathway to KSU admission. OLLI members find community and continued growth. DiscoverU campers explore what their future could look like.



5

Accessible and affordable
We offer payment plans, workforce funding, and financial assistance options. OLLI membership keeps enrichment courses affordable for adults 50 and older.



6

Support at every step
Our team is here to help you find the right program and stay on track — whether you're enrolling in a certificate, registering for an OLLI course, applying to the IEP, or signing a student up for summer camp.





Student Story
Real Learners, Real Career Moves


            "The most valuable part of my experience was the flexibility of the course. I was able to still work full-time, be with my children, and complete the certification."
          
KRISTINA LINDSEY, Human Resources Management SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP


          Whether you're earning a certificate, learning English, exploring a hobby, or sending a teen to camp — KSU CPE is built to help people at every stage move forward.
        















          Explore Our Certificates
        

          Whether you are changing careers, upskilling for your current role, or learning for fun,
          KSU Community and Professional Education has a path for you.
        




Featured Certificates
Professional Certificates with Strong Career Outcomes

            These high-demand certificates are a great place to start if you are focused on
            changing careers or advancing in your current field.
          


Project Management Certificate
Build the skills to lead projects on time and on budget.
View Project Management Certificate


Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate
Train for hands-on culinary roles in restaurants, catering, and professional kitchens.
View Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate


Medical Assisting Certificate
Train for clinical and administrative responsibilities in healthcare settings.
View Medical Assisting Certificate


















          How to Get Started with KSU CPE
        






Professional Certificates
Career-focused, non-credit certificates and workforce development for adult learners.



1

Explore certificate areas.
Browse healthcare, IT, business, legal and culinary arts programs that match your career goals.



2

Talk with an Enrollment Advisor.
Get answers about course requirements, schedules, and which certificate supports your next step.



3

Review funding options.
Learn about payment plans, workforce funding, and employer tuition assistance.



4

Register and begin.
Complete registration online and get ready for your first class, in-person or online.





              Email Professional Courses
            





Intensive English Program (IEP)
Academic English preparation for international students seeking university admission or language proficiency.



1

Submit your application.
Complete the IEP Application and Policy Agreement Form. Students under 18 must also submit a parent/guardian waiver.



2

Take the placement exam.
New students complete a placement test, writing sample, and oral interview to determine their starting level.



3

Secure your visa (if applicable).
F-1 visa students will receive an I-20 from KSU. Part-time options are available for non-F-1 students.



4

Attend orientation and begin.
All new students attend a mandatory orientation before their first 8-week session.





              Email IEP Admissions
            





OLLI — Lifelong Learning (50+)
College-level courses, social events, and enrichment programs for adults 50 and older.



1

Browse the current catalog.
Explore courses in art, language, history, technology, fitness, finance, and more.



2

Pick up an OLLI membership.
An annual membership unlocks access to all OLLI courses and special events for 12 months.



3

Register for your courses.
Sign up online, call our enrollment team, or come by in person. New sessions start four times a year.



4

Show up and enjoy.
No prerequisites, no grades — just curious people learning together at the KSU Center.

Want to learn more about Kennesaw State University?




At Kennesaw State University, we believe in empowering you to become the best version of yourself. Through a blend of rigorous academics, vibrant campus life, and diverse opportunities, you’ll discover your passions and unlock your potential.
Engage with access to over 400 student organizations.
Find camaraderie in our on-campus residence halls. Savor award-winning dining options.
Experience the thrill of competition in our club sports and NCAA Division I teams.
Become a proud Owl and a part of a supportive community that values your unique voice and ambitions.
When you choose KSU, there are no limits to who YOU will become.





Are you looking for information on Graduate Programs at Kennesaw State?
KSU offers over 80 graduate-level programs from master's to doctorate degrees in the
                                          areas of business, education, engineering, health and human services, lab sciences,
                                          management, social sciences and humanities, and technology.
REQUEST INFORMATION FOR GRADUATE PROGRAMS AT KSU









 

                                             
Request Undergrad Information
















Who will you become?

Choosing a college is not only about where you will spend the next few years studying.
                           It is about finding a place that speaks to you authentically and allows for your growth
                           and belonging. More than a name on a diploma, your college choice should reflect your
                           values, passions, and aspirations. At KSU, we believe in surrounding you with the
                           resources and people who can inspire, challenge, and support you in becoming the best
                           version of yourself -- personally, academically, and professionally. Take the next
                           step to joining Owl Nation!

KSU Research Impact




Kennesaw State University
Research








Serving Georgia Through Research




Kennesaw State University is dedicated to creating knowledge that improves the lives
                                    of all Georgians.
At KSU, we are leading the charge in the fight against opioid abuse, ensuring veterans
                                    receive the care they need, and building a world where people with diabetes can check
                                    their blood sugar without drawing blood.
Our innovations do not just stay in the lab or sit on a shelf. We work to maximize
                                    our impact by partnering with local and regional stakeholders, ensuring we reach those
                                    in need.
Around the world, ordinary people face extraordinary challenges. These challenges
                                    drive our research. Our research turns questions into progress.
Submit Research Topic
partner with ksu








 


Improving Health, Saving Lives
Dedicated to creating healthier futures for all.
Enhancing Human Capability
Guiding mechanical advancements with human capability.
Understanding Our World
Working to understand the world around us.
Innovation Through Creativity
Harnessing our creativity to advance arts and human knowledge.


 







Improving Health, Saving Lives














Kennesaw State researchers providing opioid disorder training

As Georgia navigates a widespread opioid addiction crisis, Kennesaw State University researchers are training budding nurses in addressing substance-use disorders. 
“With these funds dedicated to our four priorities, we have a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the lives of Georgians affected by the opioid crisis."
learn how KSU is fighting the opioid crisis













AMES continues VA-funded partnership to prevent veteran suicide

The partnership between the Center for the Advancement of Military and Emergency Services
                                    (AMES) Research and Georgia Department of Veterans Services has led to the completion
                                    of more than 7,000 suicide assessments across 134 counties in Georgia.
“Our collaborative, community-focused work is crucial to ensure Georgia’s veterans get the right help — where they are — when they need it."
learn how KSU is serving those who serve



















Enhancing Human Capability














KSU researcher advancing non-invasive glucose monitoring system

GlucoCheck is a ring-like sensor that uses light absorption technology to estimate
                                    glucose levels without using blood samples, providing a user-friendly alternative
                                    to finger pricks.
“We are excited about how this device will help people with diabetes, which affects about one in every 10 people in the United States."
learn how KSU is easing the burden on people with diabetes













Kennesaw State researchers developing AI-powered drones to protect peanut farms from
                                       wildlife

The team’s mission is to create a low-cost, AI-driven solution that deters destructive wildlife from farmland without the need for traditional fencing or human patrols.
“We’re giving (farmers) a tool that lets them rest at night while knowing their fields are protected. The feedback we’ve received from farmers so far has been overwhelmingly positive."
learn how KSU is helping Georgia's farmers



















Understanding our World














KSU researcher building device to allow real-time monitoring of water quality

The project, which is a collaboration between the City of Chattahoochee Hills and
                                    the West Atlanta Watershed Alliance, combines real-time monitoring with AI-driven
                                    forecasting to predict spikes in bacteria contamination before they occur.
“The bacterial forecasting system helps everyday people by ensuring cleaner and safer water. By improving water quality and reducing contamination risks, it protects public health and enhances recreational experiences."
learn how KSU is bringing real-time monitoring to Georgians













KSU researcher developing electronic nose to sniff out foodborne illness

The device is designed to detect pathogens such as salmonella and E. coli, eliminating
                                    the guesswork in identifying contaminated food.
“Food safety is a really important issue for the public, and I realized that millions of people are affected by foodborne illness each year."
learn how KSU is advancing food safety












 









Innovation Through Creativity











 





Kennesaw State looks to bring Interactive Research Methods Lab to high schools

The award-winning Interactive Research Methods Lab (IRML) helps students learn how
                                    to start with a research topic and map out the steps of a research project.
“The less resources your school district has, the more useful Hopscotch for AP Research and the Air-Lab is going to be for you."
learn how KSU is providing Georgia high schoolers with research tools













Kennesaw State and Georgia Tech researchers partner to combine dance and science

Researchers at Kennesaw State and Georgia Tech partnered to teach movement to artificial intelligence through improvisational dance, culminating with a first-of-its-kind performance:  artificial intelligence — in the form of an avatar projected onto a screen — improvising movement with human dance partners. 
“The combination of both dance and science provides limitless discoveries, and with the advanced technology that we have today this combination can be explored in depth.”
learn how KSU is blending dance with innovative technology



















How Can KSU Research Improve Your Community?

Help shape the future of real-world outcomes from Kennesaw State research. Use this form to share ideas for new research topics, community needs, emerging challenges and trends, or innovation opportunities you believe KSU should explore. Your input helps support the future of our research priorities, partnerships, and opportunities for developing our communities. 



By submitting your information, you consent to KSU using the information to contact
                           you via phone, text message, or email for informational and promotional purposes.

What’s New at KSU








Campus Improvements and Student Resources




See what’s new at Kennesaw State, including campus improvements, expanded housing, parking and transportation updates, and new Marietta Campus features. Learn how KSU is investing in the student experience and find resources to help you navigate these changes. 

Building a Better KSU Experience for Fall 2026







Parking

Nearly 600 New Student Parking Spaces 









New Buses

& Improved Shuttle Service to Get Around Campus









Housing

Additions and renovationsto the Kennesaw Campus














On This Page


Parking & Transportation
Housing Options

Questions & Resources















Building Momentum for the Future

Kennesaw State's momentum is the result of intentional investments guided by the University’s strategic plan, Taking Flight. From student success and academic programs to research, facilities, and partnerships,
                           KSU is strongly positioned for the future.
Meeting the Moment
Building Lasting Impact







Parking and Transportation Enhancements

With brand new buses and hundreds more parking spaces, big changes are coming to KSU
                           in Fall 2026. A new bus fleet, expanded shuttle services and routes, and nearly 600 new student parking spaces in commuter, residential and economy areas across the Kennesaw and Marietta Campuses are part of the new enhancements. Students can also take advantage of the Bikeshare Program, which is free for the first hour, and use the CobbLinc bus system at no additional cost.
Read more about parking and transportation updates
 













Quick Links:


Parking News See what’s new for Fall 2026, including parking, permits, buses and transportation updates
Early Semester Parking GuidePlan ahead for peak traffic, parking and transportation during the first weeks of
                                       the semester
Bus Tracker: Passio GO! AppTrack KSU buses in real time and view arrival times
Shuttle RoutesView Big Owl Bus routes, stops and service times for both campuses
CobbLincFind bus service between campuses and connections to local destinations
Campus Parking FAQsFind answers about permits, parking, citations and transportation services











Increased Housing Options

Over the past four years, Kennesaw State has expanded its on-campus housing options with the additions of The Summit I and Summit II for a total of 11 residence halls
                           across our two campuses. Additionally, renovations are currently underway at KSU Place,
                           which is scheduled to reopen to students in Fall 2027 with a modernized look and additional
                           beds.
Learn more about the expanded housing options
 













Quick Links:

Housing and Residence LifeFind on-campus housing options, application resources and information about living at KSU’s Kennesaw and Marietta campuses
The Summit - Housing and Residence LifeExplore The Summit and the new Summit II, suite-style housing for first-year students on KSU’s Kennesaw Campus.
LiveSafe Campus Safety appUse the LiveSafe app to arrange a safety escort from KSU Police or to have a friend
                                    or family member monitor your walk.










New Marietta Campus Features

Students returning to the Marietta Campus will find more dining options, additional transportation options, and several campus improvements designed to enhance the overall student experience.
                           Updates include the new Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center, the Marietta Market, Hornet Hub, and increased bus routes and more parking options. 
Read more about the new Marietta features







Student-Focused Campus Master Plan

From new residence halls to expanded academic and student support facilities, KSU campus infrastructure improvements  are taking shape through a wave of completed and ongoing building enhancements and projects that are transforming both campuses and positioning the university for continued growth. 
Explore our Capital Projects

Freshman and Transfer Freshman Application Steps

We are excited you are considering Kennesaw State University as your college home!
                     We hope you find this information helpful. If you have any questions about completing
                     your application for admission, you can find your counselor on the Contact Us page.
You should apply for Freshman Admission if you are:

A senior in high school, or
Graduated high school within the last 5 years and have not enrolled in another college
                        or university after graduating.

You should apply for Transfer Freshman admission if you:

Graduated from high school in the last five years, or
Attended another college and have earned less than 30 semester hours or 50 quarter
                        hours of transferable college credit.

Homeschool and Architecture applicants must meet additional requirements.
find your counselor
APPLY NOW
 



3.0 GPA Required for Fall 2027 Admission

Beginning Fall 2027, first-year students must meet a minimum GPA of 3.0 to be considered
                           for admission to Kennesaw State University.





2.5 GPA Required for Spring and Summer 2027 Admission

Students applying for Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 can be admitted under the current
                           GPA requirement of 2.5 or greater.

Required High School Curriculum
Kennesaw State recalculates high school GPA based on the 17 units of the Required High School Curriculum (RHSC). 
4 units of English | 4 units of Math | 4 units of Science | 3 units of Social Science
                                    | 2 units of same Foreign Language, 2 units of American Sign Language, or 2 units of USG approved Computer Science
Please see the USG-Freshman Admission Requirements Staying on Course: The Required High School Curriculum.
If you are a homeschool student, please complete the Homeschool Portfolio.

Testing Requirements

Kennesaw State accepts the SAT or the ACT for freshmen and transfer freshmen applicants,
                                    and beginning Fall 2027 we will also accept the CLT. Scores from the ACT and the SAT
                                    will not be combined. Applicants must meet minimum* English/Critical Reading and Math
                                    section requirements.
Test scores are required at Kennesaw State University for first-year applicants.



ACT: 18 - English or Reading | 18 Math
*Full ACT test score reports are required for any test score submissions.




SAT: 500 - Evidence Based Reading and Writing | 490 Math Section Score




CLT: 39 - Verbal and 16 - Math
*Accepted starting Fall 2027



Architecture Degree Program Applicants: 
Please note that there are higher admissions requirements for the Architecture Degree
                                    program and seats are limited. Applicants are encouraged to complete their application
                                    and submit all required documents by January 31 for admission the following fall semester.

Testing FAQs




Is KSU test-optional?  



No. First-Year students applying to Kennesaw State University are required to submit official SAT or ACT scores along with official high school
                                                transcripts. 






Are standardized SAT or ACT test scores required for admissions? 



Yes. First-Year students applying to Kennesaw State University are required to submit official SAT or ACT scores along with official high school transcripts. 






Do I need to submit official SAT or ACT scores if I have completed dual enrollment
                                       courses?


Yes. You will need to submit official test scores even if you have completed less than 30 transferable credit hours of dual enrollment coursework.  





Can I self-report my scores on my application?


Yes. You may enter your scores on the application, but we will require official scores sent directly from the testing agency before we can make a final admissions decision. Please be sure to send your test scores prior to the admissions deadline. 





How do I submit official test scores? 



Official scores must be submitted electronically by the respective testing agency. Use the following school codes to submit your official test scores:  SAT school code: 5359 ACT school code: 0833 
How to Send My SAT Scores
How to Send My ACT Scores






Does Kennesaw State University superscore?



For the SAT, we will take the highest Evidence-based Reading & Writing section and Mathematics section if there is more than one set of scores.  
For the ACT, we will take the highest ACT English or Reading and ACT Math scores if there is more than one set of scores.  
KSU doesn’t superscore SAT with ACT scores.  






If I take either the SAT or ACT more than once, what scores will you use?


We encourage you to send all your official test scores because we will utilize the
                                          top scores from various testing dates (called superscoring) to give you the most favorable
                                          scores for your admissions review.





I already sent my test scores. How do I know if you have received them?



You can check your application status via the Pathway to Enrollment Portal. In the Portal, you are provided with a checklist of items we have and have not received. If there is a green check mark next to "Official Test Scores," we have received your scores. 
Check My Application Status






Do I need to take both the SAT and ACT?


No. You only need to submit scores from one test (ACT or SAT). However, if you take both exams, you are welcome to send all scores. We will use the scores that are most favorable to you under our admissions policies. 





When should I plan to take the SAT/ACT?



We recommend that students test early! Start testing in your junior year of high school
                                             to provide sufficient time to see how you perform, if you want to consider taking
                                             a different test (ACT versus SAT), and if you would like to retest for the possibility
                                             of higher scores. Since we allow superscoring, your highest section scores will be
                                             taken from all test dates. Be sure to submit all official scores in order to receive
                                             superscoring.
Visit our First-Year Applicant Timeline to see available test dates prior to the Fall 2026 application deadline.






How can I prepare for the SAT or ACT?



Free and low-cost practice resources are available directly from College Board (for
                                             SAT) and ACT, including full-length practice tests and personalized study tools.
SAT Practice Materials from College Board
ACT Practice Materials






Does Kennesaw State accept the CLT?


Kennesaw State will accept CLT scores starting for Fall 2027 admission and beyond.












Freshman/ Transfer Freshman Application Process


Online application and feeSubmit your application and $40 application fee online by the deadline published for your desired semester of entry.
High school transcript(s)Work with your high school to send us your official* transcript(s) documenting all
                              coursework taken during your high school career. *Your official transcript(s) must come from your high school.
If you are a homeschool student, please complete the Homeschool Portfolio.
Official transcripts from high schools or colleges must be sent directly from the
                                    institution to:
Kennesaw State UniversityOffice of Undergraduate Admissions3391 Town Point Drive, MD 9111Suite 1000Kennesaw, GA 30144ksuadmit@kennesaw.edu

All college transcript(s)If you have earned any college credit (including dual enrollment credit) while in
                              high school, it is your responsibility to request that the college or university send
                              official transcripts to KSU.
Standardized test scoresKennesaw State accepts either the SAT or the ACT for freshmen and transfer freshmen applicants. Applicants must meet the minimum English/Critical Reading and Math section requirements.
















Application Fee Waiver

Submission of the application fee waiver is completed within the Common Application. Please carefully read the fee waiver qualifications within the application and be prepared to provide the name of your high school guidance counselor and your guidance counselor’s email address. NOTE: Selecting “fee waiver eligible” when you do not meet the requirements will delay processing your application. Ineligible fee waiver applicants will be required to pay the application fee before your application can be processed. 
Students should contact their high school counselor if they have questions regarding
                                    eligibility.



 


Flight to Excellence ScholarshipStudents with exceptional grades and test scores will be considered for an out-of-state
                                    tuition waiver to receive in-state tuition rates.







Home Educated Students




Applicants applying to Kennesaw State who attend a homeschool or high school not accredited by one of the accrediting associations listed below must document their Required High School Curriculum units through the submission of a curriculum packet. 
The USG recognizes accreditation from the following accrediting bodies: 

A regional accrediting association, such as the Southern Association of Colleges and
                                       Schools Council on Accreditation and School Improvement (SACSCASI). Accredited schools
                                       can be found on:
Cognia (formerly AdvancedED) website.  
Association of Christian Schools International
Georgia Accrediting Commission
Georgia Association of Christian Schools
Georgia Independent School Association
Georgia Private School Accrediting Council
Southern Association of Independent Schools

Applicants attending a non-accredited homeschool are required to complete the following steps in order:  

Complete the application.
Setup your NetID.

48 hours after applying, you will have your KSU# and NetID 


Once you have set up your NetID, access and complete the homeschool portfolio and attach the following documents:

Declaration of Intent to Homeschool

 Georgia law requires parents or guardians who teach their children at home to submit to the Georgia Department of Education (GADOE) an annual Declaration of Intent form. A Declaration of Intent must be submitted to the Georgia Department of Education within 30 days after establishment of a home study program and by September 1 annually thereafter.


Affidavit of Successful Completion 

Note: Submit with this portfolio only after high school graduation.  If your high school graduation date is in the future, your confirmation email will include a link to complete the form at that time.




Submit official SAT or ACT Scores. 
Submit official college transcripts.

                           pending official documentation or provisionally/conditionally accepted, you will not
                           qualify for financial aid.
Additionally, you must be in a degree seeking program to qualify for financial aid.
                           Non-degree programs, such as certificate programs or teacher certification add-on
                           programs, may not qualify for financial aid according to federal guidelines. For the
                           most up-to-date information, check with the Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid..







Scholarships



KSU’s scholarship portal, Scholarship Universe, opens every year on November 1 and closes on March 1, and includes a list of scholarships specifically for graduate students. To search scholarships:

Go to KSU's Scholarships website
Click on "Apply now"
Click on "Search Scholarships"
Category Search (click on the box with the + sign)
In the Class box, select Graduate from the list
Scroll to the bottom and click Search







Loans



Graduate students are eligible for the following loan programs:

Unsubsidized for $20,500 for an academic year.







Senior Citizen Waiver (KSU-62)



The Senior Citizen Tuition Waiver (KSU 62) covers tuition and certain fees for qualified
                                                      students who meet the following conditions:

The applicant must first apply for and be accepted to a graduate degree program*.
The applicant must be 62 years old as of the first week of the semester.
The applicant must be a resident of the State of Georgia.

*This waiver does not cover tuition for programs that do not follow regular graduate
                                                      tuition and fees.
Application ProcessSubmit your graduate application, any additional required materials, and application fee online by the graduate admission deadline for your desired program of interest and semester of entry.Once registered for classes, students will submit proof of age to the Office of the Bursar. Tuition and fees will be adjusted, and the waiver will be reflected in the student’s account once the proof of age is processed by the Office of the Bursar.
Visit Registrar
Apply Now














AmeriCorps VISTA




AmeriCorps VISTA (Volunteers in Service to America) members serve full-time for a year at nonprofit
                                                         organizations or local government agencies to build the capacity of these organizations
                                                         to carry out programs that alleviate poverty. After one year of service, VISTA members
                                                         qualify for the Segal Education Award (valued at approximately $7,395) to pay for

Graduate Research Assistantships


A Graduate Research Assistant works with a faculty member on a specific research project for a certain number of hours each week. In exchange, the GRA is granted a tuition fee waiver and provided a stipend. See the GRA website for more details.

Kennesaw State appoints Peter Grandjean as dean of Wellstar College of Health and Human Services


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 14, 2026

Peter W. Grandjean
Kennesaw State University has named Peter W. Grandjean dean of the Wellstar College
                     of Health and Human Services (WCHHS), effective Jan. 1, 2027.
Grandjean currently serves as dean of the College of Behavioral and Health Sciences
                     at Middle Tennessee State University (MTSU), where he has led efforts to strengthen
                     academic programs, expand community partnerships, and support student success across
                     one of the university's largest colleges.
“Dr. Peter Grandjean is an accomplished academic leader with a deep understanding of the evolving healthcare landscape and the important role universities play in preparing future professionals,” KSU President Kathy S. Schwaig said. “His commitment to student success, collaborative leadership style, and record of advancing academic excellence make him an outstanding choice to lead the Wellstar College of Health and Human Services as Kennesaw State continues its trajectory as a leading research university.”
Grandjean will lead WCHHS, which serves more than 7,000 students through nationally
                     recognized programs in healthcare, public health, social services, and related fields.
                     Working closely with faculty, staff, students, healthcare providers, and community
                     partners, Grandjean will focus on advancing academic excellence, fostering student
                     success, enhancing interdisciplinary research and collaboration, and expanding community
                     engagement opportunities throughout Georgia. He also will help shape and execute an
                     innovative vision for the college while addressing the state's growing workforce needs
                     and advancing health and wellness across the region.
“Dr. Grandjean brings a demonstrated ability to connect strategic vision with meaningful outcomes,” said KSU Provost and Executive Vice President of Academic Affairs Ivan Pulinkala. “His experience leading large, multidisciplinary colleges and his commitment to innovation, partnership, and student achievement align strategically with Kennesaw State's mission and aspirations.”
Grandjean brings three-and-a-half decades of higher education experience to KSU. Prior
                     to MTSU, Grandjean served as dean of the School of Applied Sciences at the University
                     of Mississippi and held several leadership positions at Baylor University, including
                     director of the Division of Health Professions and associate dean for graduate studies
                     and research collaborations. Throughout his career, he has worked to expand academic
                     opportunities, support faculty research, and augment connections between higher education,
                     healthcare organizations, and community partners.
An internationally recognized scholar in exercise physiology and health sciences,
                     Grandjean has authored more than 200 peer-reviewed publications and secured millions
                     of dollars in external funding. He is a Fellow of the American College of Sports Medicine
                     and has received numerous professional and academic honors throughout his career.
“Kennesaw State's commitment to innovation, student achievement, and community impact makes it one of the most exciting universities in the country,” Grandjean said. “I am honored to join the Owl family and look forward to working alongside faculty, staff, students, alumni, healthcare partners, and community leaders to build on the college's momentum and create new opportunities that advance health, wellness, research, and workforce readiness throughout Georgia and beyond.”
Grandjean earned a bachelor's degree in physical education from Anderson University,
                     a master's degree in exercise physiology from Texas Christian University, and a doctorate
                     in kinesiology from Texas A&M University.

Kennesaw State researcher brings AI lessons to life with shark teeth






Kennesaw State researcher brings AI lessons to life with shark teeth


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 13, 2026

A fossil shark tooth can tell a story about life millions of years ago. For Kennesaw
                     State University researcher Christine Wusylko, it can also help students understand
                     artificial intelligence (AI).
Wusylko and collaborators at the University of Florida recently received a National Science Foundation grant for Shark AI, a project that guides middle school science students through building and evaluating computer vision models that can classify real fossil shark teeth. The full grant is $254,000, and Wusylko received a sub-award of $24,000 to help the team expand the project to Georgia teachers and explore ways to keep it going after funding ends.
Led by University of Florida paleontologist Bruce MacFadden, the project is a collaboration
                     between paleontologists, engineers, museum educators, and educational technology researchers.
Using a free platform called Google Teachable Machine, students upload photographs of fossil shark teeth and train an AI model to classify them by species or tooth function. They then test the model’s accuracy and revise their training data when it makes mistakes.
The process helps students understand how AI learns from data and why its predictions
                     can sometimes be wrong.
“The models are made by humans, and there’s ways that we can introduce bias, either intentionally or not,” said Wusylko, an assistant professor of instructional technology in the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education.
Students also examine real fossil teeth, exploring how their shapes helped sharks
                     cut, grasp or crush food. Those hands-on experiences connect science lessons with
                     the work of researchers.
“The children are mirroring what real paleontologists are doing right now,” she said.
Inspired by her experience as a former K-12 science and technology teacher, Wusylko
                     says her research is focused on ways technology can help children learn complex STEM
                     topics.
“A lot of my research is based on some struggles I saw students have in the classroom, learning complex STEM topics.”
Her work on Shark AI also supports teachers, helping them build confidence using AI
                     in their classrooms. The project’s curriculum is freely available, and the team has also developed a related curriculum, Chewing on Change, that uses fossil horse teeth and computer vision to teach evolution and machine
                     learning.
The study is funded by  NSF #2147625  
– Story by Christin Senior

About KSU

Kennesaw State is a comprehensive university located on two suburban campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta, northwest of metro Atlanta. We are making an impact across the region, the nation and around the world. As the third largest university in Georgia, Kennesaw State has nearly 43,000 students enrolled in over 180 undergraduate, master’s, doctoral degree and certificate programs.

Privacy and Legal Notice




Kennesaw State University
Privacy and Legal Notice








Data Protection and Privacy Compliance Notice

This Notice establishes Kennesaw State University’s (“KSU”) privacy notices for both its website located at kennesaw.edu (“Site”) and in compliance with any applicable data privacy standards and legal requirements regarding the data collected, including compliance with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (“EU GDPR”). This Notice describes the type of information KSU collects from visitors to this Site, what we do with that information, and how visitors can update and control the use of information collected by this Site. 

Type of Information Collected and Why
Links to Other Websites
Security and Accuracy of Confidential Information
Sharing of Information
European Union General Data Protection Regulation (EU GDPR) Privacy Notice
Georgia Open Records Act
Data Retention

 







Type of Information Collected and Why

Kennesaw State University (KSU) is committed to ensuring the privacy of your information.
KSU collects two kinds of information on this site: 

Information that is voluntarily supplied by visiting the site and enrolling in programs
                              and
Information that is automatically collected as you navigate the site. 

Information voluntarily supplied by visitors seeking to access various features and information includes, among other things, name, address, and phone number. Any personal information that you choose to provide through the Site will be protected in accordance with the provisions of this Notice. If you refuse to provide personal data that is required by KSU in connection with one of KSU’s lawful bases to collect such personal data, such refusal may make it impossible for KSU to provide education, employment, or other requested services.
Information automatically collected includes the user’s IP address, date and time of the website access along with the web pages(s) visited. In addition, KSU may also collect any information that it receives from your web browser, including browser type and version, and operating system.  This information helps us understand aggregate uses of our site, track usage trends and improve our services. Additionally, university web sites use cookies to collect certain information. Cookies are small pieces of data that are sent by our Website to your Web browser. They are stored on your computer and are used to improve your web experience and improve the availability of web content. We may also use cookies to pre-fill forms so that you do not need to re-enter data. Accepting a cookie does not give us access to your computer or any personal information about you.







Links to Other Websites

Links within the university website may direct you to other websites not affiliated with KSU.  KSU is not responsible for the privacy practices, policies, actions, web content, services, or products of non-KSU sites to which we link. These links are not intended to, nor do they constitute, an endorsement by KSU of the linked materials.  We encourage you to read the privacy statements of other sites for assurance that their practices safeguard your privacy.







Security and Accuracy of Confidential Information

KSU does its best to reasonably ensure that the personal information obtained from
                           you is accurate. Visitors may review the information saved or submitted via the Site
                           at any time up to the point when it is purged. If there is an error in your personal
                           information, we will correct the information upon your request, which may be submitted
                           through Service Now. 
We have put in place reasonable physical, technical, and administrative safeguards designed to prevent unauthorized access to the online information we collect and use. While we strive to protect visitor’s personal information by encryption and other means, we cannot guarantee or warrant the security of the information you transmit to us, and if you choose to use the Site, you do so at your own risk. 
If you post any data within a public forum on any KSU website, that data is now public. 







Sharing of Information

KSU is committed to maintaining the privacy of your personal information. Any information submitted via the website will only be used for the purposes stated on the submission page.  KSU does not actively share personal information gathered from the Site, except:

as required by law (including but not limited to the Georgia Open Records Act);
as necessary to protect KSU interests;
as necessary to further research efforts pursuant to approvals from the appropriate
                              data stewards and the Institutional Review Board;
and/or with contracted service providers acting on behalf of the university who have agreed to protect the confidentiality of the data.  

KSU also complies with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (“FERPA”), which generally prohibits (with some exceptions) the release of education records without student permission. Please visit KSU’s FERPA website for more information.
  







European Union General Data Protection Regulation (EU GDPR) Privacy Notice

Lawful Basis for Collecting and Processing of Personal Data
Kennesaw State University is an institution of higher education involved in education,
                           research, and community engagement. For KSU to educate its students both in class
                           and on-line, engage in world-class research, and provide community services, it is
                           essential, necessary, and KSU has lawful bases to collect, process, use, and maintain
                           data of its students, employees, applicants, research subjects, and others involved
                           in its educational, research, and community programs. The lawful bases include, without
                           limitation, admission, registration, delivery of classroom, on-line, and study abroad
                           education, grades, communications, employment, applied research, development, program
                           analysis for improvements, and records retention. Examples of data that KSU may need
                           to collect in connection with the lawful bases are: name, email address, IP address,
                           physical address or other location identifier, photos, as well as some sensitive personal
                           data obtained with prior consent.
For more information regarding the EU GDPR, please review Kennesaw State’s EU General Data Protection Regulation Compliance Policy.  All personal data and sensitive personal data collected or processed by KSU under the scope of the KSU EU General Data Protection Regulation Compliance Policy must comply with the security controls and systems and process requirements and standards of KSU policies.
The majority of KSU’s collection and processing of personal data will fall under the following categories:

Processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by KSU
                              or third parties in providing education, employment, research and development, and
                              community programs.
Processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject
                              is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering
                              into a contract. This lawful basis pertains primarily but not exclusively to
research contracts.
Processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which KSU is subject.
The data subject has given consent to the processing of his or her personal data for
                              one or more specific purposes. This lawful basis pertains primarily, but not exclusively,
                              to the protection of research subjects.

There will be some instances where the collection and processing of personal data
                           will be pursuant to other lawful bases.
Where KSU Obtains Personal Data and Special Categories of Sensitive Personal Data
KSU receives personal data and special categories of sensitive personal data from multiple sources. Most often, this data comes directly from the data subject or under the direction of the data subject who has provided it to a third party (for example, application for admission to KSU through use of the Common App). 
Individual Rights of the Data Subject under the EU GDPR
Individual data subjects covered by KSU’s EU General Data Protection Regulation Compliance Policy will be afforded the following rights:

information about the controller collecting the data
the data protection officer contact information
the purposes and legal basis/legitimate interests of the data collection/processing
recipients of the personal data
if KSU intends to transfer personal data to another country or international organization
the period the personal data will be stored
the existence of the right to access, rectify incorrect data or erase personal data,
                              restrict or object to processing, and the right to data portability
the existence of the right to withdraw consent at any time
the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (established in the EU)
why the personal data are required, and possible consequences of the failure to provide
                              the data
the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling
if the collected data are going to be further processed for a purpose other than that
                              for which it was collected

Note: Exercising of these rights is a guarantee to be afforded a process and not the guarantee
                              of an outcome.
Any data subject who wishes to exercise any of the above-mentioned rights under the
                           EU GDPR may do so by submitting a Service Request with the Office of Cybersecurity.   
Website Data Collected and Why; Cookies
Please see the “Type of Information Collected and Why” section above for details regarding information collected from KSU websites and cookies.
Security of Personal Data subject to the EU GDPR
All personal data collected or processed by KSU under the scope of the KSU EU General Data Protection Regulation Compliance Policy must comply with organizational security controls, standards, processes and policies.  If you have questions about this Notice or believe that your personal information has been released without your consent or if you wish to correct information held by KSU, please contact us at via Service Now.
KSU will not share your information with third parties except as necessary to meet one of KSU’s lawful purposes. 
 







Georgia Open Records Act

As an entity of the government of the State of Georgia, KSU is subject to the provisions of the Georgia Open Records Act (ORA). Except for those records that are exempt from disclosure under the ORA, the ORA provides that all citizens are entitled to view the records of state agencies on request and to make copies for a fee.  For more information on KSU’s ORA compliance, please visit the Open Records Requests page on the Division of Legal Affairs website. 







Data Retention

KSU keeps the data it collects for the time periods specified in the University System of Georgia Records Retention Schedules. 

View examples of Student Records Retention Schedules.
View examples of Human Resources (Employment) Records Retention Schedules.

Kennesaw State University also may offer credentials such as certificates and diplomas at approved degree levels. Questions about the accreditation of Kennesaw State University may be directed in writing to the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges at 1866 Southern Lane, Decatur, GA 30033-4097, by calling (404) 679-4500, or by using information available on SACSCOC’s website (www.sacscoc.org).

Apply Now




Undergraduate Admissions
Apply Now















Please select the appropriate application to the right that pertains to your student
                                    type. Additionally, if you have already applied as an undergraduate or graduate student,
                                    please check the status of your application.
*Admissions decisions are made on a rolling basis once the application is considered
                                       complete. All remaining applications will receive an admissions decision based on
                                       the information available by the final admissions deadline for the respective term.







What Type of Student Are You?





First-Year Admission



Please use Common App if any of the following are true:

You are a student who is still in high school and without college credit.
You have earned college credit prior to high school graduation (dual enrollment credit,
                                                               AP/IB credit).
You graduated high school less than 5 years ago and earned less than 30 credit hours
                                                               of college credit (if you attended any college).

Apply Now
 



3.0 GPA Required for Fall 2027 Admission

Beginning Fall 2027, first-year students must meet a minimum GPA of 3.0 with test
                                                                  scores (ACT, SAT, or CLT) to be considered for admission to Kennesaw State University.

2.5 GPA Required for Spring and Summer 2027 Admission

Students applying for Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 can be admitted under the current
                                                                  GPA requirement of 2.5 or greater with test scores (ACT or SAT).








Transfer, Non-Degree, Readmission and Transient



Please use the GAfutures application if you are one of the following student types:

Transfer – More than 30 semester hours of transferable college credit.
Adult learner - Graduated or would have graduated high school more than 5 years ago
                                                               and, if any college credit was earned, it is less than 30 credit hours.
Non-degree – Post-baccalaureate education for personal enrichment. If you intend to earn another bachelor's degree, please select Transfer student on
                                                                     the application.
Readmission – Previously attended KSU.
Transient – A guest from another institution for one term.

Apply Now






Dual Enrollment



The Dual Enrollment Program (DEP) provides an outstanding opportunity for high school
                                                            juniors and seniors to get a head start on college. Students take college classes
                                                            in lieu of high school classes, and earn college and high school credits simultaneously.
Apply Now






Graduate



For master’s degrees, graduate certificates and online graduate programs.

Who will you become at KSU?

Kennesaw State University empowers students to seek, strive and succeed in academics and beyond. In addition to offering more than 190 degree and certificate programs in 11 colleges, KSU leads in innovative teaching and learning and boasts two beautiful campuses with 51,000+ students. Owl Nation is home to vibrant campus cultures, close enough to Atlanta for students to explore exciting events, fun activities, and coveted career opportunities. We’re excited that you’ve chosen KSU as your academic doorway to reach your future potential and purpose.      Our number one priority at KSU is our students and their success. KSU offers majors
                              in STEM fields, nursing, arts, cybersecurity, business, and many more. Enjoy apartment-style

We offer graduate degrees in multiple fields that are flexible, affordable, and accredited graduate programs. 

Before you begin the application process, please be aware of the following:


There is a $60 non-refundable application processing fee.*


New applicants will be asked to create a login for the application portal. This login
                                    will also be used to upload documents, check the receipt of supplemental materials
                                    and check the status of your application.


The online application should be used:


For those seeking admission to the Graduate College for the first time.


For previous or current KSU graduate students who are pursuing a different program
                                          or degree level (e.g., Certificate, Masters, Specialist, or Doctorate).




NOTE: For those who have been previously enrolled as a KSU Graduate student and wish to
                              continue in the same program,** but have NOT taken classes in the last 3 semesters
                              (your status is inactive), please complete the Readmission Form.

Graduate College Admission Requirements:


Completed online Graduate Application
$60 non-refundable application processing fee*
Official transcripts from each college or university attended. If the institution
                                 is outside the U.S., an international credential evaluation will be required. Applicants must not send international transcripts directly to Kennesaw State University.
Bachelor's degree from a Regionally Accredited college or university with a minimum
                                 GPA of 2.75
Additional requirements by program

*Application fee may vary by program**For doctoral programs, please complete a new application
NOTE: Master of Science in Data Science and Analytics was formerly Master of Science in
                                 Applied Statistics and Analytics. If you apply prior to July 1, apply to MS Applied
                                 Statistics and Analytics.

Kennesaw State University Open House

You are invited to attend Kennesaw State University's Open House!
Open House offers you the opportunity to learn more about your major and your desired
                              field of study. You will also receive information on admission requirements and financial
                              aid, and you will have the chance to hear from current KSU students.
Open House is hosted on both campuses on different days. Sign up for the campus that
                              hosts your major, and we can't wait to see you at Open House!
When planning all Enrollment Services events, every effort is made to avoid scheduling
                              them on any religious holidays or standardized testing dates. Unfortunately, based
                              on available resources, some events may be held on a religious holiday or standardized
                              testing dates. We will always have multiple opportunities to attend a tour, Open House,
                              and other Enrollment Services events for our guests to experience KSU.

Fall Dates




Saturday, October 24, 202610:30 a.m.Kennesaw Campus
Sign Up




Saturday, November 14, 202610:30 a.m.Marietta Campus
Sign Up




Find Your Campus By Your Degree
 

 

Spring Dates

Spring 2027 dates will be announced in December!










5 reasons to attend KSU’s Open House



Experience the Campus "Fit"
You can’t judge a college’s atmosphere by reading a brochure or looking at a website. You have to visit in person. Walk the campus and see the facilities. Many current students said they decided to apply because Kennesaw State just “felt” right.
Check out Housing
Explore your housing options — an in-person visit makes planning what to bring to your future home a whole lot easier. You’ll also see how living on campus provides easy access to resources, activities and events.
Delicious Food!
Enjoy a complimentary lunch in our award-winning dining facilities provided for up
                                       to three visitors.
Explore Scholarships and Aid
Figuring out financial aid can be a challenge. At Open House, financial aid counselors
                                       will answer questions and help you understand the types of aid, grants and scholarships
                                       available. Come learn about FAFSA, HOPE, student work and much more.
Learn about Majors and Programs
You can pick from academic sessions based on KSU’s colleges. You will get a feel for what KSU courses and faculty are like, and you can ask questions about degrees or academic opportunities.









Visit our Campus!

Visiting campus is a great opportunity to explore KSU and learn about Owl Nation.
Kennesaw State is a student-centered, research-driven university with a vibrant campus
                           culture and an entrepreneurial spirit. As Owls, we are guided by a purpose and, no
                           matter how we change, grow, or evolve, we never forget who we are. Welcome to Owl
                           Nation!
 
Schedule a Tour!
 




Marietta Campus







Kennesaw Campus






Upcoming Open House and Tours

Weapons, flares, fireworks, pepper spray, and smoke devices
Use of e-cigarettes, vapes, juuls, dip, chew, etc.
Illegal substances, drugs, and chemicals of any kind

High School Group Tours 




Kennesaw State University has two dynamic campuses and divides programs between the
                              two, creating unique opportunities and atmospheres for students tailored to their
                              studies.
KSU’s Marietta Campus houses many of the University’s STEM programs – focusing on innovative engineering, architecture, and science practices. The Kennesaw Campus includes majors in business, education, health services, humanities, and arts. Both
                              campuses feature award-winning dining halls, on-campus student housing, active student
                              organizations and activities, and state-of-the-art academic facilities.









Have Questions?

Contact our Group Tour Team! grouptours@kennesaw.edu 470-KSU-INFO (470-578-4636)  







We invite you to join us on a campus tour – of Marietta to learn about the future of STEM or Kennesaw to experience future leaders of business, education, and more.







Group Tour Expectations









 










Schedule a High School Group Tour

Reserved for prospective students in 9-12th grades, our high school group experience is a walking tour intended for groups of more than 10 to a maximum of 40 people.  All group high school tour requests must be made at least one month in advance. Group tours are confirmed on a first come, first served basis. A group visit request does not guarantee a visit on your requested date; all visits must be confirmed and are subject to availability.
While we cannot guarantee a tour for your group, we will make every effort to accommodate
                                    your needs. Due to high demand, if your group visits campus, we cannot offer another
                                    tour in the same academic year.


Fall 2026 Group Tour Dates are full.  Spring 2027 Group Tours will be available for registration in December.


For all other groups, we encourage you to explore our virtual or self-guided campus tour. 
Explore our Virtual KSU Experience










 FAQs








When are group tours?


Group tours are offered Monday through Friday at 10:30 a.m. on both the Marietta and
                                                   Kennesaw Campuses. Please note that group tours are not offered during certain holiday
                                                   weeks or on special event days for the University. While we do not offer Saturday
                                                   tours, groups are also welcome to come to our Saturday Open House events. Please email
                                                   grouptours@kennesaw.edu for more information.





When do you start booking group tours?


Group tours for the Fall Semester can be booked starting the last week of July.  Spring Semester group tours can be booked starting in mid-November. We make every effort to accommodate your group; however, groups are booked on a first-come first-served basis. 





How many students can I bring with my group?


We offer walking tours for groups of 10 - 40 high school-age students. 





How many chaperones do I need to have with my group?


We request one adult per every 10 students. 





How long is the tour?


The tour is typically 60 minutes. It includes a walking tour of campus and a Q & A with the tour guides. 













Can my group eat lunch on campus?



The ability to eat in our award-winning dining halls is available. Your group tour must be confirmed to receive the needed information to make a reservation with our dining halls. Please note that all payments must go through Dining. The Undergraduate Admissions Office is not responsible for any payment of your group’s meals.
Visit University Dining to request your group dining reservation






Can I bring my middle school or elementary school group?



Due to the great demand for guided group tours and limited available staffing, we
                                                      are only able to offer guided group tours to prospective students that are in 9th
                                                      grade and above. However, we can provide groups below 9th grade with a virtual tour
                                                      of our campuses.

Take a Virtual Tour!

 






Do group tours see Housing?


Kennesaw State University takes pride in providing a safe community to current residents and students. Therefore, group tours are not authorized to enter student resident halls. The University works hard to keep the integrity of our residential spaces clean and safe. 





Is there a charge for a group tour?



There is no charge for a tour of campus.  
There is a charge to eat lunch on campus. Please note that the Undergraduate Admissions Office is not responsible for any payment for your group’s meals. All payments must go through Dining. Visit University Dining to see all the menu items. 






What if it rains?



We will still have the tour and try to keep your group inside as much as possible.
                                                      Plan to dress accordingly for the weather and wear comfortable walking shoes.
Campus events are subject to cancellation due to inclement weather. You will be notified
                                                      via email and/or phone should a cancellation occur. Special weather statements can
                                                      also be viewed on the Kennesaw State University website. Should the University be
                                                      closed, all campus tours and events will be canceled.

Open Doors to New Possibilities

Your gift helps KSU students achieve their full potential.
Kennesaw State University's most important mission is putting our students first by
                              providing them with a world-class education and fulfilling campus experience. Gifts
                              to scholarships and student support services enable students from diverse backgrounds,
