Kennesaw State researcher earns prestigious NSF CAREER Award
October 02, 2026
Kennesaw State University Associate Professor of Software Engineering Nasrin Dehbozorgi has received a National Science Foundation Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER) Award, one of NSF’s most prestigious honors for early-career faculty. The award will support her work advancing STEM education through a novel agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework.  
Read More











Kennesaw State researcher receives NIH Grant to study sleep apnea
October 01, 2026
Kennesaw State University researcher Shumit Saha has received a $235,520 grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to develop artificial intelligence tools that analyze snoring patterns to identify where the upper airway collapses during sleep and predict whether patients may respond to hypoglossal nerve stimulation.
Read More











Ph.D. student advances research regarding AI integration with devices with limited computing power
September 29, 2026
In the artificial intelligence (AI) era, hospitals can leverage AI to uncover valuable insights from patient data, but privacy requirements and devices with low computing capabilities present hurdles to widespread adoption. At Kennesaw State University, Ph.D. student Nazmus Shakib Shadin is studying how hospitals can help train AI while keeping records private and using the equipment they already have.
Read More











Kennesaw State researcher developing safer, more efficient computing systems for intelligent vehicles
September 24, 2026
Modern vehicles are becoming computers on wheels, powered by increasingly complex software and artificial intelligence. As those systems take on more responsibility, they must process information quickly and reliably enough to keep critical functions running safely.
						Kennesaw State University computer science researcher Kun Suo is working to improve how those systems operate through a $356,782 National Science Foundation (NSF) grant focused on developing more efficient and secure computing infrastructure for intelligent vehicles.
Read More











Kennesaw State software engineering student develops AI-powered navigation system
September 11, 2026
For Kennesaw State University software engineering student Robert Hoeh, finding a room inside an unfamiliar building could one day be as simple as asking a question.
			Hoeh is helping develop an AI-powered augmented reality navigation system that lets users ask for directions and guides them through complex indoor spaces. The technology could improve accessibility for people with cognitive disabilities while also helping first responders navigate unfamiliar buildings more quickly.
Read More











Student research into AI-powered crop monitoring system aims to prevent plant loss
August 26, 2026
According to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization, plant pests and diseases destroy up to 40% of crops worldwide each year, threatening jobs and the global food supply. 
						Kennesaw State University computer science major Brendan Miller is working on technology that could help farmers catch those problems before they spread. 
Read More











Kennesaw State professor earns Texas Innovator's Award for AI platform supporting student success
July 22, 2026
Kennesaw State University assistant professor Sagnik Dakshit, of the College of Computing and Software Engineering, has earned a Texas Innovator's Award for developing an artificial intelligence-powered platform that supports student success. 
						He received the honor for creating VTA, or Virtual Teaching Assistant, a tool designed to provide personalized academic support while helping instructors improve learning outcomes.
						
Read More











From personal tragedy to innovation: Professor advances virtual reality grief support
July 14, 2026
Shaped by experience navigating loss and grief, a Kennesaw State University researcher is leveraging emerging technologies that could improve access to community and support for bereaved parents.  
			Funded by a two-year grant from the National Science Foundation, Lei Zhang, a human-computer interaction researcher in College of Computing and Software Engineering, is building a virtual reality system that lets bereaved parents meet, share memories, and process grief together in a shared immersive digital space, inspired by his own experiences losing a child to cancer. 
Read More











Ph.D. student finds AI can detect warning signs of global oil crises before they happen
July 07, 2026
As geopolitical conflicts continue to disrupt global energy markets, Kennesaw State University Ph.D. student Nzubechukwu Ohalete found that artificial intelligence (AI) can identify warning signs of major oil crises weeks before they occur.
Read More











Kennesaw State awards first computer science doctoral degrees
May 11, 2026
This month marks a landmark achievement for Kennesaw State University as it celebrates the graduation of the first two students from the new doctoral program in computer science, established in 2022. 
Read More

Kennesaw State researcher brings AI lessons to life with shark teeth
October 13, 2026
A fossil shark tooth can tell a story about life millions of years ago. For Kennesaw State University researcher Christine Wusylko, it can also help students understand artificial intelligence (AI).
						Wusylko and collaborators at the University of Florida recently received a National Science Foundation grant for Shark AI, a project that guides middle school science students through building and evaluating computer vision models that can classify real fossil shark teeth.
Read More











Kennesaw State professor earns national award for contribution to education
August 07, 2026
Kennesaw State University professor Erik Malewski has received a national award for his decades of contribution to teaching and learning. 
			A professor of curriculum studies in the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education, Malewski has been selected to receive the Curriculum & Pedagogy Group Lifetime Award. The national honor recognizes scholars whose careers have made lasting contributions to curriculum and pedagogy through scholarship, mentorship, and leadership.
Read More











KSU student helps bring a fresh approach to music education using colors
June 23, 2026
As a child, Kennesaw State University student Laurin McCoy loved music but struggled to understand traditional music notation. While she learned to play the piano by ear, the experience left her saddened that children might never discover or develop their musical talents simply because they were unable to read music. Years later, McCoy found an opportunity to help address that challenge through research.
Read More











Bagwell College of Education hosts 2026 Georgia Elementary Science Olympiad
June 15, 2026
Kennesaw State University’s Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education recently welcomed nearly 1,300 elementary school students representing 63 schools for the Georgia Elementary Science Olympiad State Tournament. 
Read More











'Triple Owl' turns passion for teaching into doctoral success
June 11, 2026
For high school chemistry teacher Ashley Thomas, coming back to Kennesaw State University to earn a third post-graduate degree was an easy decision. 
			A science teacher in DeKalb County Schools, Thomas is now a ‘Triple Owl,’ having previously earned a master's and education specialist degree in instructional technology, and now a Doctor of Education in Instructional Technology. So for her, KSU – in particular, the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education – felt like home. 
Read More











Kennesaw State, Fulton County Schools teaming to create pathways into teaching careers
April 14, 2026
Kennesaw State University and Fulton County Schools are partnering to create new opportunities for high school students to accelerate their college education and pursue careers in teaching.
			
			Through the dual enrollment initiative, Fulton County students can earn college credit while in high school, gain early classroom experience, and have a streamlined admissions process into Kennesaw State’s Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education. Leaders from Fulton County Schools and Kennesaw State signed the agreement during a ceremony on Tuesday at KSU.
Read More











NSF-funded project explores the use of AI-powered chatbots to prepare future educators
April 01, 2026
Funded by a three-year, $300,000 National Science Foundation grant, Associate Professor of Instructional Technology Dabae Lee developed an AI-powered agent system that simulates student interactions. The aim is to give pre-service teachers practice in “responsive teaching,” which is the ability to elicit and interpret students’ thinking and to extend their mathematical ideas by questioning.
Read More











Associate professor, CrossFit athlete finds strength in motion while navigating multiple sclerosis 
March 13, 2026
About ten years ago, Jennifer Wells stepped off a boat while visiting Robben Island in South Africa. She immediately felt what she describes as ‘pins and needles’ in her feet, a pervasive pain she thought was due to her cramped sitting position on the vessel. She thought it would go away in a few hours, but it didn’t. The symptoms only got worse, leading to numbness.
									For Wells, an associate professor of higher education and student affairs at Kennesaw State University, that episode marked the beginning of her journey with multiple sclerosis (MS), a journey of resilience that has taken her to the world stage as a CrossFit adaptive athlete. 
Read More











Marrielle Myers elected next president of the Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators
February 27, 2026
Marrielle Myers was recently elected president of the Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE), the largest professional organization devoted to improving mathematics teacher education. AMTE includes more than 1,000 members, including professors, researchers, and policy experts, who focus on the professional development of K–12 mathematics teachers.
Read More











Georgia Highlands College and Kennesaw State University expand transfer pathways
February 25, 2026
Georgia Highlands College (GHC) and Kennesaw State University (KSU) are expanding their LINK partnership, a collaborative initiative to create seamless transfer pathways and expand academic opportunities for students.
Read More

Engineering student creates robotic hand designed to track patient health
October 09, 2026
A robotic hand capable of grasping a patient’s wrist and measuring vital signs may sound futuristic, but Kennesaw State University mechatronics engineering student Daksh Garg is already bringing the concept to life through research in robotics and biomedical sensing.
						The Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology student is building a 3D-printed robotic hand equipped with sensors designed to collect health information while interacting with a person. 
Read More











Kennesaw State researchers receive NSF grant to advance soft robotics education
October 08, 2026
Soft robots that can bend, flex, and safely interact with people are becoming more common in research and industry. However, many engineering students still have little exposure to the technology. Kennesaw State University researchers are working to change that with the support of a recent National Science Foundation (NSF) grant.
Read More











Engineering student uses NASA data to study distant star systems
October 07, 2026
Kennesaw State University electrical engineering student Thi Tran never imagined herself conducting astronomy research. Now, she is using data from a NASA satellite to help researchers distinguish distant planets from stars that can produce nearly identical signals.
Read More











Engineering student combines technical and marketing skills through hands-on experiences
October 05, 2026
Kennesaw State University student Cynthia Konziase is building a versatile skill set by combining industrial and systems engineering with marketing and hands-on industry experience through opportunities within the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology (SPCEET).
Read More











Student cooks up success through engineering and content creation
September 28, 2026
When Kennesaw State University engineering student Joel Louise began creating cooking videos this summer, he knew very little about preparing meals or producing social media content. What he did understand was how to analyze a problem, learn from mistakes, and improve a process.
						Louise developed those skills through KSU’s First-Year Scholars Program, an early research experience he credits with inspiring his approach to content creation. 
Read More











Kennesaw State rises in U.S. News rankings of top universities
September 23, 2026
Kennesaw State University continues to rise in stature among the nation’s universities while earning a top spot in Georgia for undergraduate engineering programs, according to the U.S. News & World Report 2027 Best Colleges rankings released on Sept. 22.
Read More











Hornet Hub gives Kennesaw State competition teams space to build, innovate
September 18, 2026
Kennesaw State University celebrated a new chapter in hands-on learning with the official opening of the Hornet Hub on the Marietta Campus. The 12,000-square-foot facility provides student competition teams, which design and build projects for regional and national competitions, dedicated space and resources to bring their work from concept to completion.
Read More











Kennesaw State student developing robotic rehabilitation arm inspired by family experience
September 08, 2026
Watching his grandfather lose mobility after a traumatic accident gave Kennesaw State University student Kai Clifford a firsthand look at how difficult everyday movement can become. Now, the senior mechanical engineering student is using robotics research to explore ways rehabilitation could become more comfortable and effective.
Read More











Mechatronics engineering student uses AI-powered system to keep waterways clean
July 30, 2026
It is estimated that up to 23 million metric tons of plastic enter waterways each year, according to the United Nations Environment Programme. While harmful materials continue to plague governments around the world, a Kennesaw State University student is developing an artificial intelligence-powered system to detect litter before it reaches the ocean.
			
			Mechatronics engineering student Saam Grami is creating a system that detects, classifies, and tracks floating litter in rivers. 
Read More











Kennesaw State professors use NSF grant to strengthen semiconductor education through interactive learning
July 29, 2026
As the United States works to strengthen its semiconductor industry, Kennesaw State University researchers are helping prepare the next generation of engineers. 
						Through a National Science Foundation-funded project, they are using interactive visualizations to make one of electrical engineering's most challenging subjects easier for students to understand.
Read More

Kennesaw State appoints Peter Grandjean as dean of Wellstar College of Health and Human Services
October 14, 2026
Kennesaw State University has named Peter W. Grandjean dean of the Wellstar College of Health and Human Services (WCHHS), effective Jan. 1, 2027. 
Read More











Nursing professor earns inaugural fellowship focused on nurse retention
October 12, 2026
From pediatric and school nursing to academia, Kennesaw State University assistant professor Alyson Epp has made a career of working with younger people. 
			
			Her research into retaining nurses and professional identity among nurses helped make her the first recipient of the Jane J. Yarbrough Nursing Fellowship in KSU’s Wellstar School of Nursing. Epp earned the fellowship, which began with the Fall 2026 semester, for her expertise in professional practice and retention.
Read More











Kennesaw State names nursing simulation lab in honor of Katherine Scott
October 06, 2026
Kennesaw State University has honored longtime donor Katherine A. Scott by naming a nursing simulation lab in recognition of her $1 million gift establishing the Katherine A. Scott Nursing Scholarship Endowment.
Read More











Kennesaw State student publishes study on alcohol's impact on Ugandan women
September 10, 2026
Few undergraduates can add “lead author in a peer-reviewed journal” to their list of accomplishments. Kennesaw State University student and Harry S. Truman Scholarship finalist Allisa George is one of them.
									
									George, an Honors student double majoring in public health and biology, is the first author of a National Institutes of Health-funded study examining alcohol and mental health among women in Uganda recently published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 
Read More











Kennesaw State appoints Tracy Fasolino as associate dean, Wellstar School of Nursing director
August 06, 2026
Kennesaw State University has named accomplished nursing educator and healthcare leader Tracy Fasolino, Ph.D., as associate dean and director of the Wellstar School of Nursing (WSON) and professor of nursing, effective Aug. 1.
Read More











From KSU Owl Network to FIFA World Cup, alumna builds sports media career
July 08, 2026
In preparation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Kennesaw State University alumna Maddie Crews ’24 marked her calendar for 49 consecutive days of covering the competition for multiple media outlets.
Read More











Wellstar College launches first study abroad program to Amsterdam, providing a transformative global experience for KSU students
July 02, 2026
Kennesaw State University's Wellstar College launched its first Amsterdam study abroad program, giving students immersive global public health experiences through research, cultural engagement, and experiential learning.
Read More











AOPA announces 2026 Howard R. Thranhardt Award recipients, including Kennesaw State's Dr. Mark Geil
June 23, 2026
AOPA announces 2026 Howard R. Thranhardt Award recipients, including Kennesaw State’s Dr. Mark Geil
Read More











Twins who grew up at Kennesaw State graduate as nurses
June 18, 2026
Katelyn Dockery remembers being pre-school age, sitting in her father’s office after school, coloring on a white board with markers. Her twin sister Taylor recalls going to Kennesaw State University basketball games and getting her face painted in the lobby at VyStar Arena.
						
						Their father, KSU Faculty Director of General Education in KSU’s Office of Academic Affairs Chris Dockery, remembers it all — basketball games, afternoons spent in his office with his daughters, taking them to lunch at The Commons, among other activities. And 21 years later, the Dockery family has cemented its legacy at KSU, with a pair of new graduates.
Read More











Kennesaw State researchers examine Atlanta's World Cup moment
June 11, 2026
Situated in the Atlanta metropolitan area, Kennesaw State University has a loge-level seat to one of the premier sports cities in the U.S.
						
						Owl alumni work in the administrative offices of nearly every Atlanta professional sports team and sporting venue in the area, thanks in large part to the education they received at Kennesaw State. Many have studied under the tutelage of faculty in the Department of Exercise Science and Sport Management, the latter integrating their personal research interests to set up students for success beyond the classroom.
Read More

Alumna earns competitive scholarship to study in Japan
September 25, 2026
It was a trip to Japan during high school that sparked Leah Hackaday’s curiosity about how other countries operate and interact with each other, a curiosity that eventually led her to major in international affairs when she enrolled at Kennesaw State University. The opportunity to spend a semester in Japan during her junior year at KSU only grew her interest in the country. 
									Today, thanks to earning a competitive scholarship from the Japanese government, Hackaday, a graduate of KSU’s School of Government and International Affairs, has now begun studying for a master’s degree in international affairs at Waseda University in Tokyo. 
Read More











Kennesaw State rises in U.S. News rankings of top universities
September 23, 2026
Kennesaw State University continues to rise in stature among the nation’s universities while earning a top spot in Georgia for undergraduate engineering programs, according to the U.S. News & World Report 2027 Best Colleges rankings released on Sept. 22.
Read More











KSU associate professor honored with 2026 Georgia Civic Excellence Award
September 17, 2026
For his efforts to strengthen and protect democracy, Kennesaw State University political science associate professor Eric Castater has been honored with a 2026 Georgia Civic Excellence Award from the Georgia Democracy Resilience Network.
Read More











Two KSU students trade the Gold Dome for Capitol Hill
August 24, 2026
Six months ago, Jada Barronton and Saideep Chilukuri answered phones in House and Senate offices under the Gold Dome. Over the summer, they both helped track legislation and conduct policy research for U.S. congressional offices on Capitol Hill. 
									The two Kennesaw State University students, who received the university’s D.C. Owls Scholarship, spent their summer interning in Washington, and both credit a semester at the Georgia State Capitol with helping them succeed.
									
Read More











Kennesaw State student explores how children respond when adults lie
July 31, 2026
By age 6, most children know that lying is wrong. But what do they think when adults lie, especially someone they trust like a parent?
						Kennesaw State University psychology student Charlie Clement is examining how children ages 6 to 11 interpret lies told by people with varying levels of authority. 
Read More











Greece study abroad challenges KSU students to tell stories of the past with bones
July 28, 2026
In a small village on the island of Crete, just southeast of mainland Greece, anthropology major Jess Drilling learned to identify signs of osteoarthritis in skeletal remains, helping piece together the stories of people who walked the earth centuries ago.
									Drilling is one of four Kennesaw State University students who spent part of their summer at an archaeological research center, studying human skeletal remains dating from the fifth to seventh centuries to uncover clues about how people lived, what they ate, and the injuries and illnesses they experienced. 
Read More











Record number of Gilman Scholars at Kennesaw State travel the globe
July 24, 2026
Aaliyah Uchendu is one of a record number of KSU students awarded the Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship this year. The Gilman Scholarship is a prestigious award funded by the US State Department that provides recipients up to $5,000 to support study or internships abroad; only about 20%-25% of applicants are selected for the award. 
Read More











Journalism student plying her craft as a World Cup photographer
June 29, 2026
As a young soccer player growing up in Georgia, Sofia Cupertino never imagined that one day she would be standing on the sidelines of a FIFA World Cup match, camera in hand, photographing some of the game's biggest stars on the world’s biggest stage.
						Now a journalism student in Kennesaw State University’s Norman J. Radow College of Humanities and Social Sciences, Cupertino is covering World Cup matches in Atlanta this summer with Soccer Down Here (SDH), an Atlanta-based soccer media outlet. 
Read More











Anthropology student explores digital tipping and customer behavior
June 26, 2026
As a barista, Alexandria Nottage has witnessed many customers hesitate whenever the digital payment screen asks whether they would like to leave a tip. Those daily interactions got Nottage thinking about how tipping had changed from a voluntary gesture of appreciation into something many customers now feel expected to do.
			To find out, Nottage, a Kennesaw State University anthropology major, conducted a research study examining how digital tipping influences customer behavior and perceptions. 
Read More











KSU study explores how childhood trauma affects body and mind
June 16, 2026
Traumatic events in childhood do not only leave emotional scars. Sometimes, they leave biological ones too.
						Saloni Patel, a first-year psychology major at Kennesaw State University, is studying how adverse childhood experiences — commonly known as ACEs — leave a measurable biological mark that can affect how we think, focus, and learn. Her research examines whether inflammation triggered by early-life stress contributes to the cognitive struggles some students face in the classroom.
Read More

Kennesaw State researcher brings AI lessons to life with shark teeth
October 13, 2026
A fossil shark tooth can tell a story about life millions of years ago. For Kennesaw State University researcher Christine Wusylko, it can also help students understand artificial intelligence (AI).
						Wusylko and collaborators at the University of Florida recently received a National Science Foundation grant for Shark AI, a project that guides middle school science students through building and evaluating computer vision models that can classify real fossil shark teeth.
Read More











Engineering student creates robotic hand designed to track patient health
October 09, 2026
A robotic hand capable of grasping a patient’s wrist and measuring vital signs may sound futuristic, but Kennesaw State University mechatronics engineering student Daksh Garg is already bringing the concept to life through research in robotics and biomedical sensing.
						The Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology student is building a 3D-printed robotic hand equipped with sensors designed to collect health information while interacting with a person. 
Read More











Kennesaw State researchers receive NSF grant to advance soft robotics education
October 08, 2026
Soft robots that can bend, flex, and safely interact with people are becoming more common in research and industry. However, many engineering students still have little exposure to the technology. Kennesaw State University researchers are working to change that with the support of a recent National Science Foundation (NSF) grant.
Read More











Kennesaw State researcher earns prestigious NSF CAREER Award
October 02, 2026
Kennesaw State University Associate Professor of Software Engineering Nasrin Dehbozorgi has received a National Science Foundation Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER) Award, one of NSF’s most prestigious honors for early-career faculty. The award will support her work advancing STEM education through a novel agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework.  
Read More











Kennesaw State researcher receives NIH Grant to study sleep apnea
October 01, 2026
Kennesaw State University researcher Shumit Saha has received a $235,520 grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to develop artificial intelligence tools that analyze snoring patterns to identify where the upper airway collapses during sleep and predict whether patients may respond to hypoglossal nerve stimulation.
Read More











Student cooks up success through engineering and content creation
September 28, 2026
When Kennesaw State University engineering student Joel Louise began creating cooking videos this summer, he knew very little about preparing meals or producing social media content. What he did understand was how to analyze a problem, learn from mistakes, and improve a process.
						Louise developed those skills through KSU’s First-Year Scholars Program, an early research experience he credits with inspiring his approach to content creation. 
Read More











Kennesaw State researcher developing safer, more efficient computing systems for intelligent vehicles
September 24, 2026
Modern vehicles are becoming computers on wheels, powered by increasingly complex software and artificial intelligence. As those systems take on more responsibility, they must process information quickly and reliably enough to keep critical functions running safely.
						Kennesaw State University computer science researcher Kun Suo is working to improve how those systems operate through a $356,782 National Science Foundation (NSF) grant focused on developing more efficient and secure computing infrastructure for intelligent vehicles.
Read More











Recent NIH grants aim to improve parasite research, acquire crucial instruments
September 21, 2026
Kennesaw State University researcher Soon Goo Lee recently secured two National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants to advance parasite research and expand the university's biomedical research capabilities through new instrumentation.
			
			The assistant professor of molecular biology earned an R16 grant from the NIH’s National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) to continue his study of an essential enzyme, called PMT, in protozoan parasites in hopes of finding an attackable weak spot for therapies that treat parasitic diseases. 
Read More











Kennesaw State students expand research horizons in India
September 14, 2026
While growing up in Guatemala, David Roque Perez saw several of his relatives battling cancer with limited access to treatment and therapies. So, for the Kennesaw State University biology major, spending the summer in India researching treatments for lung cancer not only built on his growing passion for research but also his goal of improving access to care in Guatemala.
Read More











Kennesaw State student publishes study on alcohol's impact on Ugandan women
September 10, 2026
Few undergraduates can add “lead author in a peer-reviewed journal” to their list of accomplishments. Kennesaw State University student and Harry S. Truman Scholarship finalist Allisa George is one of them.
									
									George, an Honors student double majoring in public health and biology, is the first author of a National Institutes of Health-funded study examining alcohol and mental health among women in Uganda recently published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 
Read More

So, for the Kennesaw State University biology major, spending the summer in India researching treatments for lung cancer not only built on his growing passion for research but also his goal of improving access to care in Guatemala.

									George, an Honors student double majoring in public health and biology, is the first author of a National Institutes of Health-funded study examining alcohol and mental health among women in Uganda recently published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 
Read More











Research into muscular degeneration wins top prize at Birla Carbon Symposium
September 04, 2026
Kennesaw State University biology student Pedro Santos’ research project on muscular degeneration in fruit flies won the top prize at the 2026 Birla Carbon Scholars Symposium.
Read More











Physics and mathematics double major explores theory and experiment in summer research experience
August 31, 2026
Caitlyn Garrett has sampled both experimental and theoretical physics in her time at Kennesaw State University. This summer, the physics and mathematics double major combined the two during a research experience at Louisiana State University.
Read More











Brain research leads to publications on THC exposure, Alzheimer's drugs
August 27, 2026
Kennesaw State University researcher Vishnu Suppiramaniam is advancing understanding of brain health across the lifespan, joining collaborators in publishing studies that examine the harmful effects of prenatal THC exposure and a promising Alzheimer's disease treatment.
Read More











Research consortium leads to opportunities for Kennesaw State students
July 31, 2026
In March of this year, Kennesaw State University joined the Oak Ridge Associated Universities, a consortium of more than 170 universities that collaborate on research initiatives, share resources, and help place students in federal research opportunities at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee.
			
			Junior chemistry major Miriam Raggs is spending this summer conducting research at Oak Ridge, through the lab’s Research Student Internship (RSI) program, thanks in part to this association but also thanks to her research mentor, Assistant Professor of Chemistry Madalynn Marshall.
Read More











Chemistry students engage in research through KSU lab's NSF C-CAS affiliation
July 27, 2026
Like many college students, Kennesaw State University senior Lilianna Kocai and junior Genevieve Insalaca have spent their summer surrounded by a buzzing cohort of friends – without leaving campus.
			
			The two chemistry students have spent the summer synthesizing fluorescent compounds and running computer-assisted simulations in the laboratory of KSU Associate Professor of Organic Chemistry Carl Saint-Louis. Their work is part of an innovative program funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) that involves computer-assisted programming as another method of experimentation. 
Read More











Mosquito research draws KSU environmental science major to the woods for the summer
July 23, 2026
Kennesaw State University senior Brooklyn Galvan has found a happy place for the summer – in the mosquito-infested woods near Hattiesburg, Mississippi.
			
			The environmental science major is conducting research into mosquitoes as pollinators as part of the National Science Foundation’s Research Experiences for Undergraduates for Gulf Coastal Plains Ecology. The experience builds on Galvan’s experience researching the importance of mosquitoes to the ecosystem in the lab of KSU Assistant Professor of Microbiology Andrew Haddow.
Read More











Physics student enriches knowledge at National High Magnetic Field Laboratory
July 21, 2026
Kennesaw State University physics student Matt Bonvissuto has taken what he has learned on campus to the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory in Tallahassee, Florida, on a Research Experiences for Undergraduates project funded in part by the National Science Foundation.
Read More

We are KSU

Kennesaw State is a comprehensive university located on two suburban campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta, northwest of metro Atlanta. We are making an impact across the region, the nation and around the world. As the third largest university in Georgia, Kennesaw State has over 51,000 students enrolled in over 190 undergraduate, master’s, doctoral degree and certificate programs.


















 
 
 
 

KSU at a Glance

 
 
 
 







KSU Owls Create Their Own Legacy

Kennesaw State University is focused on growth, transformation and tenacity. This is our legacy. As one of Georgia’s largest research-driven universities, we put our students first – to empower them to seek and strive to discover their own path forward. We are KSU Owls and together, we ascend.

Our Mission and Vision

Kennesaw State University transforms lives through academic excellence, innovative

Kennesaw State will achieve national prominence as a public university known for education,

Leadership

We strive to collaborate with our campus community to grow Kennesaw State’s undergraduate and graduate programs, while supporting research efforts across the disciplines.

Top Majors

What We Care About at KSU



Student-Centered Success
Our students’ success is the reason for all we do here at KSU.
Research with Relevance
As an R2-designated research-driven university, we embrace exploration that delivers

Learning through Engagement
Collaboration is at our core – students, staff and faculty work hand-in-hand to inspire a culture of supportive, engaged learning.
Future-Ready Graduates
Our graduates are more than career ready – they’re ready to make an impact in our communities, our nation and around the world.
Power of Perspective
Our diverse backgrounds and experiences produce a collaborative spirit that opens

Our students become innovators, complex thinkers and societal leaders.

Merit Pages Highlight Kennesaw State Students’ Achievements

Using the online platform Merit Pages, Kennesaw State University students can share
                        their accomplishments with friends and family, as well as create a profile to impress
                        future employers. Students receive an email each fall inviting them to activate their
                        official KSU Merit page.
Kennesaw State automatically updates students’ Merit pages with accomplishments such as making dean’s or president’s lists, earning scholarships, presenting research at a conference, studying abroad, or participating in student competition teams. In addition, students can customize their profile pages with pictures, work and school experience, and awards earned.
To learn more about Merit Pages and to see published stories, visit Kennesaw State’s Merit site.
Following are answers to some frequently asked questions about the platform:




How do Merit Pages benefit students?



Merit creates a personal record of each student’s academic career, showcasing achievements and activities. A Merit page also is useful for seeking a job, with options to upload a résumé and list employment history.
Hundreds of colleges around the country use Merit Pages to recognize and promote student success, so Owls who opt in will join a national network of college students. Also, Merit updates are shared with students’ high schools, hometown news outlets and state legislators.
Merit pages can be connected to social networks such as Twitter, Instagram or LinkedIn,
                                          ensuring that friends and family are able to see and learn about the great activities
                                          students are participating in and being recognized for at Kennesaw State.






How does Merit work?



Merit is an automated email system managed by KSU Strategic Communications and Marketing.
                                          When students earn recognition, the University publishes a personalized article to
                                          Merit and sends it to the hometown newspapers, high schools and government officials
                                          of each student involved.
Each time new content is added to their Merit page, students receive an e-mail with a link to view their story and share their achievements with friends and family. Parents also receive an email allowing them to share their students’ accomplishments on their own social media channels.






How do students update or customize their Merit pages?


After a student logs into their personal Merit page, they can create a customized
                                       URL, add a profile picture and bio, and connect to their social media profiles. They
                                       also can make changes to personal information such as email address, hometown and
                                       major.





How is students’ privacy protected?



Kennesaw State respects students’ privacy. The content KSU shares through Merit includes only information about students that is designated as “directory information" under the Federal Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA).
Student pages are set by default to be private and are not searchable on kennesaw.meritpages.com, unless students adjust their profile settings to make their pages searchable. However, stories containing students’ first and last names automatically will be shared with hometown news outlets, high schools and state legislators.






How can students opt out?



Opting out removes a student’s profile from Merit Pages and prevents the University from publishing future achievements by that student. Students can opt out at any time by following these instructions from Merit.

KSU adds new buses, more parking spaces for Fall 2026 semester


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Aug 17, 2026
With brand new buses and hundreds more parking spaces, big changes are coming to Kennesaw State University this fall. 
Students returning for the Fall 2026 semester will find a new bus fleet, streamlined routes and hundreds of additional parking spaces, designed to make travel to, from and between the University’s two campuses more reliable.
                     A new circulator bus route will transport passengers around the Marietta Campus.


The improvements are part of KSU’s efforts to improve parking and transportation services and will feature 26 buses, including four brand new buses, serving the Kennesaw and Marietta campuses, parking areas and other key destinations. The fleet now includes four environmentally friendly hybrid buses, 12 35-foot buses, six 29-foot buses, and four 20-seat buses. 
“Transportation plays an important role in the daily campus experience, and these improvements are designed to make getting around KSU easier and more dependable,” said Kelly Johnston, executive director of Campus Services. “From modernizing our fleet to increasing service in high-demand areas, we are continuing to look for ways to better serve our students, faculty and staff.” 
Students can stay up to date on parking and transportation upgrades through the Parking and Transportation News page. The Early Semester Parking Guide is a go-to resource for parking and transportation information during the first few
                     weeks of the semester.
Since the start of the spring semester, KSU has added or converted almost 600 student parking spaces across both campuses — roughly 300 per campus. For the Kennesaw Campus, that includes a new student economy lot opening this fall at 1000 Gutenberg Drive, with a Big Owl Bus shuttling students to campus.
Beyond replacing buses, KSU has reworked routes to reduce travel and wait times. Stops
                     that are close enough to walk between are being consolidated, allowing buses to move
                     more quickly from the shuttle lots to campus and between Kennesaw and Marietta.
The Kennesaw-Marrietta route will now make stops at only: the Student Recreation and Activities Center and The Commons on the Kennesaw Campus, and the Joe Mack Wilson Student Center on the Marietta Campus. As a result, students will experience a reduction in trip and wait times. A new circulator route, the Marietta Loop, will take students around the Marietta Campus so that the Kennesaw-Marrietta buses can focus on moving students between campuses. 
Students can follow buses in real time through the Passio GO! app, available for both iOS and Android. After selecting Kennesaw State, riders can
                     view routes, bus locations and the number of passengers aboard, which can help them
                     anticipate whether an approaching bus may be full. The app also lists service start
                     and end times instead of scheduled departures.
KSU’s partnership with CobbLinc has also added more options. Students can now ride four CobbLinc routes at no charge when their trips begin on the Kennesaw or Marietta campus by
                     showing their KSU ID. The MyStop app provides CobbLinc bus locations and route information.
With thousands of students returning this fall, Johnston recommends budgeting extra travel time during the first three weeks of the semester. 
“Planning can make a big difference during the start of the semester,” Johnston said. “Allowing additional travel time, using the upper levels of the parking decks and becoming familiar with the Big Owl Bus system can help everyone begin the semester more smoothly.”
Here are some more tips for a smoother start to the semester:
●      Use the Early Semester Parking Guide, a great resource to help with transportation and parking as you ease into the semester. 
●      Give yourself extra travel time the first three weeks, especially on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
●      Head to the upper levels of parking decks; spots are usually easier to find. 
●      Drive slowly and stay alert in the parking decks during class changes.
●      Download Passio GO! for live Big Owl Bus routes and passenger counts.
●      Use MyStop for CobbLinc routes and don't forget your KSU Talon Card for free rides.
●      Avoid citations by purchasing a permit, park in your assigned area, and keep your plate visible (no pull through parking). 
●      For short trips, try KSU Bike Share. Rides under an hour are free through the Movatic app.
●      Take advantage of our walkable campuses and walk when it's convenient.
For a comprehensive look at important back-to-school information, and strategic investments
                     and improvements made across the University visit the What's New at KSU page.

Kennesaw State adds more on-campus housing for students


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Aug 13, 2026

The Summit I and The Summit II
Kennesaw State University is expanding its on-campus housing options for students
                     by opening a new residence hall for the 2026-27 academic year and renovating an existing
                     residential community.
The Summit II, a 462-bed, nearly 97,000-square-foot facility in the heart of the Kennesaw Campus,
                     welcomes its first residents this fall. The addition of Summit II reflects priorities outlined in Kennesaw State’s “Taking Flight” strategic plan to support student engagement and enhance the student experience inside
                     and outside the classroom.
“This new residence hall represents more than a building,” said Chris Bruno, executive director of KSU Housing and Residence Life. “It reflects our continued commitment to student success, community, and creating spaces where Owls can live, learn, and thrive.”
Kennesaw State has now opened two new residence halls in the past four years. The
                     Summit II features common areas, study rooms, and an outdoor courtyard that connects
                     with neighboring The Summit I, which opened in 2022.
Across campus from Summit I and II, the KSU Place residential community is undergoing
                     a complete renovation. The project includes updating the heating-air conditioning,
                     plumbing, electrical systems, siding, and flooring, installing new furniture, modernizing
                     the kitchens and bathrooms, and making the facility more energy efficient.
Also, a reconfiguration of the rooms will result in 265 additional beds. When KSU
                        Place reopens with a new name in Fall 2027, Kennesaw State will have 6,639 beds for on-campus students across 11 residential communities.
“The renovation to KSU Place enables us to grow our on-campus inventory without building a brand-new building,” Bruno said. “It's going to be a beautiful community.”
For a comprehensive look at important back-to-school information, and strategic investments
                     and improvements made across the University visit the What's New at KSU page.

Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center

Kennesaw State University, Marietta Campus

Overview
The Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center is a 70,000-square-foot interdisciplinary research and teaching facility on Kennesaw State University’s Marietta Campus. The center, which officially opened on April 24, is designed to accelerate innovation and entrepreneurship, foster collaboration across disciplines, and translate research into real-world solutions that benefit communities beyond campus.
The Shore Innovation Center brings together faculty from multiple colleges, encouraging
                     daily interaction among experts. External partners also are invited into the space
                     as collaborators, helping ensure research is grounded in real-world needs.
Purpose and Vision

Created to address complex, real-world challenges that transcend individual disciplines
Built to shorten the path from discovery to application
Emphasizes collaboration among faculty, students, and external partners
Supports KSU’s mission to advance society through bold, collaborative discovery

Key Features

Interdisciplinary research labs located side by side, with a focus on community impacts
Shared research spaces and modern computing resources
Flexible classrooms that support hands-on and collaborative learning
Home to the Doug and Robin Shore Entrepreneurship and Innovation Center, where research, student ideas, and corporate needs intersect

Student Experience

Students work alongside faculty on active research projects
Learning goes beyond lectures to include hands-on, real-time problem solving
Exposure to interdisciplinary teamwork mirrors how work happens outside academia
Prepares students with collaboration, communication, and adaptability skills valued
                        in the workforce

Marietta Campus to feature new dining, transportation, and campus upgrades this fall






Marietta Campus to feature new dining, transportation, and campus upgrades this fall


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Aug 11, 2026

Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center
Students returning to Kennesaw State University’s Marietta Campus this fall will find more dining options, new bus routes, and several campus improvements designed to enhance the overall student experience.
Leading the updates is the opening of the Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center. Officially opened in April, the new facility serves as a hub for interdisciplinary
                     research while also providing students with a place to study, gather, and recharge
                     between classes.
Because the Shore Innovation Center is centrally located on campus, it creates a natural gathering place for students to study, collaborate, and connect,” said Lee White, associate vice president of business services. “It was thoughtfully designed to be more than just a building; it’s an inviting hub where students can come together, engage with one another, and feel connected to the campus community.”
Inside the Shore Innovation Center, students will discover a new retail concept, The
                     MRKT, which will offer Haymaker Coffee and Dunkin' products and pastries. It will
                     also feature fresh grab-and-go meals from EatKSU and a milkshake machine. Students will also find two new dining concepts inside the
                     Joe Mack Wilson Student Center. The Local Spot, located next to Dunkin', will feature
                     a rotating lineup of local restaurants, while High Roller Sushi will replace the previous
                     sushi concept with fresh, elevated menu offerings.
"The No. 1 goal is to respond to student feedback," White said. "Marietta students
                     want more variety and more options, and they want experiences that are unique to their
                     campus."
KSU’s Campus Services gathered feedback through dining surveys, conversations with students, and regular
                     meetings with the Student Government Association. The input helped shape new concepts
                     unique to the Marietta Campus.
Across campus, near the Engineering Technology Center, another structure has transformed the landscape. Officially opened in June, the 12,000-square-foot Hornet Hub will serve as the newest collaboration space for KSU’s award-winning student competition teams, including the Night Owl Racing team, aerial robotics competition team, and hydraulic bike team, among others.
Getting around campus will also become easier this fall with the launch of a new Big
                     Owl Bus circulator route that continuously loops around the Marietta Campus Monday
                     through Friday. The shuttle will make it easier for students to travel between academic
                     buildings without having to walk across campus between classes.
"We've never offered that service before in Marietta," White said. "It creates more
                     mobility options around campus and helps students get from one end of campus to the
                     other more effectively and efficiently."
Students driving to the Marietta Campus will also benefit from approximately 300 additional
                     parking spaces created through lot reconfigurations, along with resurfaced parking
                     lots that improve both functionality and the appearance of campus. Classroom renovations
                     are also underway in the Architecture Building, Atrium Building, and the Engineering
                     Technology Center.
Looking ahead, White said the university will continue listening to students as future
                     improvements are planned.
"We can't wait to welcome them back to campus this fall and see everything that we've
                     been working on over the last several months," she said.
For a comprehensive look at important back-to-school information, and strategic investments
                     and improvements made across the University visit the What's New at KSU page.
– Story by Raynard Churchwell
Photo by Darnell Wilburn Jr.

KSU bolsters infrastructure to support student experience, University’s growth






KSU bolsters infrastructure to support student experience, University’s growth


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Aug 12, 2026

A rendering of the planned renovations to the Carmichael Student Center on the Kennesaw
                           Campus.
From new residence halls to expanded academic and student support facilities, Kennesaw State University’s Campus Master Plan is taking shape through a wave of completed and ongoing projects that are transforming both campuses and positioning the university for continued growth. The work reflects KSU’s broader campus planning strategy: place programs in spaces that best support their needs, renew aging facilities and infrastructure, and sequence renovations, relocations, and new construction so that each project helps create opportunities for the next.
A physical feature of that growth is the growing skyline and expanding footprint on
                     both the Kennesaw and Marietta campuses, with the latest completed project, The Summit II residence hall, providing 462 additional beds for KSU students. The Summit II joins the Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center and the Hornet Hub on the Marietta Campus as completed projects for the upcoming school year, all of which with a common component — they support student success at KSU.These enhancements build on parking and transportation updates, including a new bus fleet, expanded shuttle services and routes, and more than 600 new parking spaces. 
“At the end of the day, it’s about creating the best possible experience for students,” said Julie McDaniel, the university architect in the Office of Planning, Design and Construction. “By grounding our planning in that objective, we can prioritize projects that make a meaningful difference in students’ daily lives. I’m happy to help bring people together around that shared vision.”
With the aforementioned projects now complete, KSU is continuing work on three other
                     projects. The ongoing renovation of Kennesaw’s Carmichael Student Center will be “transformative for the students in that space,” McDaniel said. The strategic renovation includes an expanded student commons; updated student hubs such as workshop areas, offices and meeting rooms; a new game room, new atrium stairs to connect the second and third floors, renovated restrooms, and updates to fire alarm and smoke evacuation systems. The total renovated area is approximately 45,000 square feet.
During construction, University Rooms are offline, but CARE Services will continue
                     to provide resources for students. The Campus Print Shop and Student Mail Services
                     have relocated to the second floor near the bookstore. The new-look student center
                     is slated to reopen fully in Fall 2027.
An ongoing project is the renovations to existing classrooms in the Architecture Building,
                     the Atrium Building, and the Engineering Technology Center in Marietta, which will
                     reconfigure less used smaller classrooms to much needed flexible large classrooms.
Finally, the KSU Place residence hall is also under construction which will provide
                     a complete renovation and modernize the buildings, including updated HVAC, plumbing,
                     electrical systems, siding, and flooring. Students will also see completely updated
                     kitchens and bathrooms, as well as new furniture and improved sidewalks.
Scheduled to reopen in Fall 2027, KSU Place will see an additional 265 beds following the renovation, bringing the total number of beds on KSU's campuses to 6,639 across 11 residential communities.
The Campus Master Plan also includes new facilities for KSU Athletics, including the Wellstar Center for Sports Excellence. The state-of-the-art sports performance and sports medicine facility is designed to support the University’s growing athletics program and more than 400 student-athletes. Located adjacent to Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, the facility will provide high-performance training, strength and conditioning, sports medicine, rehabilitation, hydrotherapy, nutrition, and related athlete-support spaces. The project is part of KSU’s broader partnership with Wellstar Health System and complements the renovation of the Wellstar Champions Complex for football operations, creating an integrated athletics and sports-performance environment.
These projects are part of a larger sequence of campus improvements. Rather than addressing
                     facilities individually, KSU is coordinating projects so that renovations and relocations
                     can unlock space for other institutional priorities.
Other upcoming construction projects include the Research Support Building, further additions to the Geer College of the Arts District at Chastain Pointe, expansion of administrative and support facilities at 1000 Gutenberg Drive, and two more building renewals to improve the student experience in Marietta – repurposing the Administration Building to a Student Success Center and the Textiles Building for the College of Architecture and Construction Management academic spaces.
McDaniel noted the expansion of Planning, Design and Construction team and credited
                        her colleagues for facilitating the myriad projects that will help KSU meet the demands
                        of a growing student body.
“We’ve made strategic moves to allow for more growth,” she said. “It’s a long sequence of projects, but they work together. As one program moves into a space that better supports its needs, that creates an opportunity to solve another space need somewhere else on campus.”
For a comprehensive look at important back-to-school information, and strategic investments
                     and improvements made across the University visit the What's New at KSU page.

Certificates
 Certificate in Accounting - Undergraduate







Certificate in Accounting 



Experience the financial intricacies with the Accounting Graduate Certificate program at Kennesaw State University. Designed to empower individuals seeking to expand their expertise in the field of accounting, this comprehensive certificate program offers a glance into the landscape of financial practices and principles.    While all of the classes offered in this certificate program are on the undergraduate level, you will obtain the required prerequisite courses for the Coles College MBA Accounting Concentration. You will also gain an understanding of advanced accounting methodologies, financial reporting, auditing and taxation strategies. This certificate program not only equips you with theoretical knowledge but also hones your practical skills, enabling you to apply your learning to real-world scenarios and industry challenges.  Fostering a dynamic learning environment that encourages critical thinking, collaborative problem-solving, and ethical decision-making, you will gain essential traits for success in the dynamic field of accounting. 







Earning this certificate satisfies the accounting prerequisites for students entering
                                             the MBA program accounting concentration.
All classes in this certificate program are undergraduate courses.

Kennesaw State University
Degrees and Programs
Certificates
Certificate in Coaching Education - Undergraduate 







Certificate in Coaching Education 

The Certificate in Coaching Education addresses the pressing demand for competent and skilled coaches. Coaches acquire the ability to have a positive influence on the lives of young individuals, illustrating the significance of teamwork, the rewards of diligence, and the connection between effective strategies and outcomes both on and off the field. This educational program is structured to equip aspiring coaches with the aptitude to engage with athletes spanning diverse age groups and skill levels. It encompasses everything from physical readiness to comprehending the emotional, social and cognitive necessities of athletes.   Upon completion of this undergraduate certificate program, you will possess the essential knowledge, abilities and professional skills needed to step into an introductory coaching role within educational institutions, sports clubs, community initiatives, colleges and various levels of athletic establishments.   The curriculum of the Certificate in Coaching Education is designed in accordance with the National Standards for Sport Coaching, as outlined by SHAPE America. It encompasses elements of physical education pedagogy, health promotion, injury prevention, and the foundational principles of kinesthetics in preparing athletes for optimal performance.  
 














Program Snapshot

Program Format: Face to Face Number of Credit Hours: 18  Entry Term: Fall, Spring, SummerTime to Complete: No Time Limit

Kennesaw State University
Degrees and Programs
Certificates
Certificate in Diversity & Community Engagement - Undergraduate







Certificate in Diversity & Community Engagement Certificate

The Certificate in Diversity and Community Engagement educates you about the theory
                        and history of diversity concerns (national and global) as these relate to interdisciplinary
                        study and praxis. You will take courses that focus on regional and global diversity
                        concerns that are likely to impact their choices of community action and/or career;
                        one course will require them to develop their own engagement project focused on social
                        justice issues.
This certificate is designed for students in a wide variety of majors interested in studying diversity issues from an interdisciplinary perspective while also participating in a hands-on community engagement project. This certificate will also explore mental health issues and holistic therapies through an interdisciplinary framework. Specifically, you will explore mental health issues and holistic therapies through an interdisciplinary framework and participate in outreach projects to marginalized communities to address suicide ideation, the use of nonprescription drugs/substances, and other social problems. 


 












Program Snapshot

This program is a part of the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities and Social Sciences.

                        fundamental questions related to the use of geographic information systems (GIS).
                        GIS is a computer-based mapping technology that visualizes, edits, manipulates and
                        analyzes spatial data and imagery for decision-makers. GIS is an essential tool in
                        understanding what is where; it is used in urban and regional design, marketing and
                        industrial location, transportation, precision agriculture, forestry, environmental
                        systems, engineering, emergency services, epidemiology, crime analysis, and utilities,
                        among other applications. The certificate can be completed in class or online.
Students must earn a “B” or higher cumulative grade in all the required courses, with a “C” or higher grade in each course.

Certificate in Intelligence and Homeland Security

If you’re looking for a program that will arm you with the knowledge of the politics of major governments around the world, so that you may be a more informed and empowered global citizen that can foster connections with other cultures and protect your own country, then the certificate in Intelligence and Homeland Security is designed for you!
The Intelligence and Homeland Security Certificate examines the operations and processes
                        of the agencies connected with the U.S. Intelligence Community and those of U.S. Homeland
                        Security. Your coursework will explore the response practices of the Homeland Security
                        Administration and the procedures of Politics in the U.S. Intelligence Community.
                        This certificate will help you understand the nature of crisis management, appropriate
                        responses and the resulting impact on society.

You must meet the criteria for acceptance into the Nonprofit Leadership Alliance Certificate program (see Campus Executive Director). Completing this Certificate’s requirements can also result in you receiving national credentialing (Certified Nonprofit Practitioner).

Communication
Marketing, & Public Relations
Cultural Competency & Diversity
Financial Resource Development and Management
Foundations and Management of the Nonprofit Sector
Governance, Leadership & Advocacy
Legal & Ethical Decision Making
Personal & Professional Development
Program Development
Volunteer & Human Resource Management
Future of the Nonprofit Sector

Certificate in Six Sigma Green Belt - Undergraduate







Six Sigma Green Belt Certificate

Industrial engineers and other professionals are often asked to champion organizational
                        efforts to improve performance in some areas. These activities are referred to as
                        Process Improvement or Continuous Improvement initiatives and are the focus of the
                        Six Sigma methodology. It is not unusual for management in any organization to want
                        to improve performance even if Six Sigma is not a formal program within the company.
                        A Green Belt is a professional level of recognition for individuals trained in Six
                        Sigma. This certificate is based on the American Society for Quality (ASQ) Six Sigma
                        Green Belt body of knowledge. The courses in the certificate provide education in
                        quality system principles, methodology and standards.
Student outcomes:

Demonstrate knowledge of statistics for quality control 
Effectively demonstrate quality concepts and ideas 
Work successfully in team environments 
Identify and manage quality projects

Kennesaw State University
Degrees and Programs
Certificates
Certificate in Workplace Interpersonal Relationships – Undergraduate







Certificate in Workplace Interpersonal Relationships – Undergraduate




Learn the peacebuilding skills needed to successfully navigate interpersonal relationships
                                 in constantly changing workplace environments. At Kennesaw State University, you can
                                 earn a Workplace Interpersonal Relationships Certificate (WIRC). Learn to be an effective
                                 leader and make these sought-after skills stand out on your resume.

The five undergraduate courses (16-semester hours) will teach you the theories, concepts, and principles underlying conflict and its causes. You’ll also learn:

To understand the different perspectives of those in conflict.
To develop mutual understanding.
To produce positive change, particularly in challenging environments.

How To Earn Your Workplace Interpersonal Relationships Certificate
KSU Students
This Certificate is available to any KSU undergraduate student, regardless of major. Current KSU students can add the certificate in Owl Express using the “Declare or Change Major/Minor” link under the Student Records tab.  Interested students are encouraged to first talk with your academic advisor, as the required courses may be allowed as electives in some undergraduate programs. 
Non-KSU Students

KSU faculty members have also helped six other Georgia colleges and universities add this Certificate. Prospective certificate students from a cooperative institution can participate in any member’s WIRC program without having to go through an additional undergraduate admissions process.
For all other non-KSU students who are interested in the Certificate, you will need
                                 to apply to KSU as an undergraduate student. On the application, select this certificate
                                 as the program of interest.
For more information, please use the email or phone number below.

Certificate in American Studies - Graduate







American Studies Certificate

The Graduate Certificate in American Studies covers the history and cultural interaction
                        of the United States and the Americas, focusing on the relationships between policy,
                        labor dynamics and cultural expressions. You will engage in coursework to study the
                        literature and culture of America in a global context, the societal patterns of the
                        American economy and community and significant movements in American history. This
                        graduate certificate includes 15 hours of graduate course work and can be taken along
                        with another KSU graduate program, like a graduate minor, or it can be taken as a
                        standalone certificate.
Additionally, you will complete assignments that provide an overview of important
                        questions, methods and theoretical approaches in contemporary American Studies literary
                        scholarship as well as an advanced introduction to important literary works.


 












Program Snapshot

This program is a part of the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities and Social Sciences.

Certificate in Business Intelligence - Graduate 







Certificate in Business Intelligence

The Business Intelligence Certificate at Kennesaw State will educate you on business
                        intelligence concepts and techniques for analyzing data and presenting actionable
                        information to inform managerial decisions. Specifically, it will equip you with various
                        tools and methodologies to examine and collect data for analysis and create reports
                        to simulate real-world systems. You will look at the vital workflow process of business
                        analysis, business intelligence simulations and operation research. This graduate
                        certificate prepares you to use business intelligence concepts and techniques for
                        presenting actionable information to inform managerial decisions in a wide range of
                        career fields.



Sign Up for Our Next Info SessionGet your questions answered at our next virtual info session for the Business Intelligence
                           certificate program.












Program Snapshot

Program Format: Face to Face
Number of Credit Hours: 15
Entry Term: Spring, Summer, Fall
Time to Complete: 12-month program
Application Deadlines: 

Fall, July 1
Summer, April 1

Admission Requirements




GPA Requirement – GPA of 3.0 or greater.
Degree Requirement – Undergraduate degree in business or related quantitative fields.
Previous Experience –Two (2) years industry work experience required.




Testing: Those with GRE/GMAT score (GMAT= [500,550], Equivalent GRE Score) above set threshold
                                    can apply for waiver of the required experience.
Those with an undergraduate GPA of 3.5 and above and coming from a business or quantitative
                                    field can apply for a waiver of the required experience.
Those with a master's degree earned from an accredited US university in a business
                                    or quantitative field with GPA of 3.0 or more can apply for an experience waiver.
International Students – You may be required to take the GMAT/GRE and satisfy the university wide Test of
                                    English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) requirement.

Certificate in Business Research Methods - Graduate




Kennesaw State University

Certificates
Certificate in Business Research Methods - Graduate







Post-Master’s Executive Certificate in Business Research Methods

This certificate in Business Research Methods is a niche doctoral-level, graduate program for senior researchers in the "insights industry". It is designed for any working professional with significant training and experience in planning, designing, conducting, and analyzing research studies and applying research skills to solve complex business problems. 
Course credits earned from this certificate may be applied to a full Ph.D. in Business
                        Administration at Kennesaw State.
This post-master's certificate will allow you to be proficient in:

Comprehensive understanding of various research designs, encompassing ethical considerations.
Development of a research strategy aligned with research questions.
Execution of research studies employing diverse methods, such as surveys, experiments,
                           archival research, and qualitative approaches.
Application of suitable statistical techniques for effective data analysis, including
                           univariate, multivariate, qualitative, and latent construct modeling.
Interpretation of research findings and formulation of business implications based
                           on the obtained outcomes.
Acquisition of practical skills in commonly used software packages, including SAS,
                           SPSS, NVIVO, and SmartPLS.















Program Snapshot

Program Format: Face-to-Face
Number of Credit Hours: 12 
Entry Term: Fall
Time to Complete: 12-month program
Application Deadline: 

Fall, July 1

Curriculum 
Apply Now










Admission Requirements

Online Graduate Application – There is a non-refundable $60 application processing fee.
Transcripts – Official transcripts from EACH college and/or university you have attended. Must be
                           in a sealed envelope from the institution or sent electronically to the Graduate College
                           (ksugrad@kennesaw.edu).
Current Resume – Submit your current resume or CV.
Previous Experience - 8 years of professional experience and have an accredited master’s degree.

Higher Education Administration Certificate

The Graduate Certificate in Higher Education Administration (HEA) is a 15-hour post-master’s professional certificate for qualified candidates who wish to pursue credentials in higher education administration. The certificate program is designed to further develop experienced leaders in the areas of HEA foundations, institutional effectiveness and marketing, organizational management, legal and ethical issues, and other areas of critical need for the twenty-first century higher education administrator. Kennesaw State University
Degrees and Programs
Certificates
Certificate in Information Security and Assurance - Graduate 







Certificate in Information Security and Assurance

The graduate certificate in Information Security and Assurance teaches you how to
                        secure and manage IT resources, and how to plan, provide and manage system security
                        incidents and disasters. You will also learn to interpret and promote IT ethics and
                        legalities (including corporate and regulatory compliance in terms of methods, approaches,
                        and governance).
This KSU certificate is designed for both working professionals and graduate students.
                        You will get to learn IT security technology through a hands-on virtual lab. The Coles
                        College of Business has the only graduate certificate in Information Security and
                        Assurance available from business schools in Georgia. This certificate emphasizes
                        the skills and knowledge necessary to protect and inspect systems, and to detect and
                        react to threats to the security of information in those systems. This certificate
                        can be completed along with the Master of Science in Information Systems (MSIS) with
                        no additional course or can be completed as a certificate.

Nurse Educator Post-Graduate Certificate 

The post-graduate certificate program is designed to cultivate the skills and knowledge
                                 necessary for individuals seeking to excel as Nurse Educators. This graduate certificate
                                 offers a comprehensive and in-depth learning experience to provide certified nurses,
                                 who have already obtained a master's degree in nursing, with the pedagogical tools
                                 and expertise needed to effectively educate the next generation of nurses.
Through advanced coursework, practical teaching opportunities, and mentorship from experienced educators, participants will develop a profound understanding of educational theories and practices. By engaging in this certificate program, nurses will expand their horizons, refine their clinical proficiencies, and foster the critical thinking and leadership skills required to thrive in the dynamic field of nursing education.  
With a focus on cultivating in teaching, utilizing the latest technologies, and staying ahead of current trends in healthcare and education, graduates of this graduate certificate program will be prepared to make a lasting impact on nursing education, contributing to the enhancement of patient care and the nursing profession.
