We offer graduate degrees in multiple fields that are flexible, affordable, and accredited graduate programs. 



New Applicants

Returning Users

Before you begin the application process, please be aware of the following:


There is a $60 non-refundable application processing fee*.


New applicants will be asked to create a login for the application portal. This login
                                    will also be used to upload documents, check the receipt of supplemental materials
                                    and check the status of your application.


The online application should be used:


For those seeking admission to The Graduate College for the first time.


For previous or current KSU graduate students who are pursuing a different program
                                          or degree level (e.g., Certificate, Masters, Specialist, or Doctorate).



Only one active application is permitted per entry term.

NOTE: For those who have been previously enrolled as a KSU Graduate student and wish to
                              continue in the same program**, but have not taken classes in the last 3 semesters (your status is inactive), please complete
                              the Readmission Form
 
Start Your Application

Graduate College Admission Requirements:

Domestic Applicants:
Graduates holding a baccalaureate degree from colleges or universities accredited
                              in a manner accepted by Kennesaw State University may apply for admission to The Graduate
                              College. Applicants must submit the credentials deemed necessary by the chosen degree
                              program. Applicants are accepted to a specific graduate program and must reapply in
                              order to change programs.

Completed online Graduate Application
$60 non-refundable application processing fee*
Official transcript/s from the college or university granting the bachelor’s degree (additional transcripts maybe be required)
Bachelor's degree from a Regionally Accredited college or university.
Additional requirements by program

 
International Applicants:
A student should apply as an International Applicant if they are:

Not a U.S. Citizen.
Currently in the U.S. on an F-1 (student) visa.
Currently living outside the U.S., and will require an F-1 visa to study in the United
                                 States.
Currently in the U.S. on any other class of visa.
In the process of applying for Permanent Residency status but have not yet received
                                 the Permanent Residency card.

In addition to meeting specific requirements for each degree program, international
                              students must meet the following additional requirements:

Completed online Graduate Application
$60 non-refundable application processing fee*
U.S. bachelor’s degree equivalent required. Official transcripts from the college or university granting the bachelor’s degree (additional transcripts may be required).  If the institution is outside of the U.S., an international credential evaluation is required. Applicants should not send international transcripts directly to KSU.
Test of English Proficiency.
                                 
                                 
Applicants from the following countries are exempt from the English Language Proficiency
                                       requirement: Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Ghana, Guyana,
                                       Ireland, Jamaica, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tobago,
                                       Trinidad, United Kingdom, United States or Zimbabwe.
Applicants who have graduated from a college or university in the United States accredited
                                       in a manner accepted by Kennesaw State University are exempt from the English Language
                                       Proficiency requirement.
Applicants not exempt by A or B above can take either of the following tests:
                                       
                                       
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) Minimum required score: Internet version (iBT) - 80 (or 4.5 on the 2026 scale)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)* Minimum required score: 6.5 





6. Additional requirements by program 
 
Additional Documentation for International Applicants:International applicants who are requesting an I-20 for an F-1 visa must submit all
                              of the following to the International Student and Scholar Services Office in order
                              to enroll at Kennesaw State University:

an affidavit of support from the sponsor
a certified financial statement from the sponsor’s bank showing that funds are available for one year of study
a valid passport

International Student and Scholar Services Office: https://www.kennesaw.edu/global-education/international-student-scholar-services/contact-us.php

Graduate Admissions
HomeAdmission Process  Dates and DeadlinesInternationalTestingTransient StudentsAppeal ProcessDouble OwlFinancial InfoGraduate CatalogGraduate CollegeFormsContact Graduate AdmissionsGet Graduate Programs Information

At KSU, we believe there is no substitute for the global enrichment provided by geographic, ethnic, racial, religious, and cultural diversity. If you’re an international student planning on applying to KSU, you should plan to have all documents in at least one month before the published deadline for your selected program. International students must meet basic international admissions requirements for their classification, and you may have additional requirements based on visa type, country of origin, and educational history.
You are considered an international student if you meet the following criteria:

You are not a US citizen or permanent resident
You live outside the US and will require an F-1 visa to study in the US
You currently live in the US on a non-immigrant visa (B1, F2, J1, J2, G, or H1, etc.)
You are in the process of applying for Permanent Residency status but have not yet
                        received your Permanent Residency card




 




Requirements for F-1, J-1, H1-B, or Permanent Resident Alien (Green Card Holder)


Completed online Graduate Application for Admission to KSU
Non-refundable $60 application processing fee, payable to Kennesaw State University
Transcripts must be evaluated by one of the following agencies      a. Evaluations must come from either an AICE or NACES accredited evaluation service.     b. Evaluations must include course-by-course and a calculation of your GPA. The evaluation must come to us in a sealed envelope or electronically directly from the agency.
Test of English Proficiency
                              
                              
Applicants from the following countries are exempt from the English Language Proficiency
                                    requirement: Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Ghana, Guyana,
                                    Ireland, Jamaica, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tobago,
                                    Trinidad, United Kingdom, United States or Zimbabwe
Applicants who have graduated from a college or university in the United States accredited in a manner accepted by Kennesaw State University are exempt from the English Language Proficiency requirement.  
Applicants not exempt by A or B above can take either of the following tests:
                                    
                                    
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) Minimum required score:  Internet version (iBT) - 80 (or 4..5 on the 2026 scale)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)*  Minimum required score: 6.5




Additional documents as required by the specific program you are applying to

IMPORTANT: Online programs are NOT eligible for F-1 Student Visa



















Other Visa Holders

If you have a non-immigrant visa other than F-1, J-1, or H-1B (such as L, E, A, K,
                                    B, etc.), please contact the Office of Graduate Admissions so an admissions officer
                                    can determine your admission requirements and enrollment eligibility.
Email
Apply










Foreign Credential Evaluations

Foreign credentials refer to transcripts from educational institutions outside the
                           United States. All applicants (domestic and international) with foreign credentials
                           are required to submit an official evaluation. An official evaluation is a review
                           of your academic documents to provide U.S. equivalency. Evaluations must include course-by-course
                           and a calculation of your GPA. Evaluations must come to us in a sealed envelope or
                           electronically directly from the agency. Please do not send international transcripts directly to Kennesaw State University.







English Proficiency

Below are the various methods you can use to meet the English Proficiency requirement
                           for admission.

Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) Minimum required score (iBT Internet version): 80 (or 4..5 on the 2026 scale)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Minimum required score: 6.5

Exemption Options:

Applicants from the following countries* are exempt from the English Proficiency requirement:
                              Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Ghana, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica,
                              Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tobago, Trinidad, United
                              Kingdom, United States or Zimbabwe
Applicants who have graduated** from a college or university in the United States
                              accredited in a manner accepted by Kennesaw State University are exempt from the English
                              Proficiency requirement.

Applicants not exempt by A or B above must take the TOEFL or IELTS test.
*Supporting documentation (i.e. copy of passport) may be requested. **Official transcripts must be on file with Graduate Admissions

HomeAdmission Process  Dates and DeadlinesInternationalTestingTransient StudentsAppeal ProcessDouble OwlFinancial InfoGraduate CatalogGraduate CollegeFormsContact Graduate AdmissionsGet Graduate Programs Information


Process for Graduate Admissions Appeals

Appeals of graduate admissions decisions at Kennesaw State University are made to
                     the Dean of The Graduate College. KSU Graduate Catalog, “Graduate Admissions.” This memorandum details the process such appeals will follow:

Notice to applicants: Applicants will be apprised of their ability to appeal admissions decisions through postings on the University’s Office of Graduate Admissions and The Graduate College’s websites, as well as contemporaneously with admissions decisions

                        
Notification of Admissions Contemporaneously with notifications of admissions decisions, applicants will be informed of their ability to appeal those decisions and directed to the University’s web resources detailing the appeals process.


The Appeal:

Basis for appeal. Appeals of admissions decisions may follow different processes based on the grounds
                                 of the appeal:

Discrimination. If the applicant believes her or his admissions decision is impermissibly based upon the applicant’s real or perceived gender identity, sexual orientation, veteran status, spiritual beliefs, physical abilities, racial and ethnic background, and economic status, the applicant may directly contact the University’s Office of Diversity & Inclusion at 470-578-2614.
Other basis.  If the applicant wishes to appeal his or her admissions decision based on other factors, the applicant needs to submit a written appeal to
                                    the Dean of The Graduate College.


Written Appeal. Within fourteen (14) days of the mailing date of the admissions decision, the applicant
                                 may file an appeal. The appeal should, at a minimum, contain the following:

An explanation of the admissions decision;
An explanation of why the applicant believes the decision was incorrect;
Identification of any evidence the applicant believes supports her or his position.
                                    The applicant may be asked to provide this information to permit The Graduate College
                                    to process his or her appeal;
Any other information the applicant believes is relevant to her or his appeal.
Effective appeals will typically involve information the applicant may not have provided in his or her original application, but which might have influenced the University’s decision regarding her or his application.
For example, following notification of an unsuccessful application, an applicant for
                                       the Master of Science in Criminal Justice might speak to a professor regarding his
                                       or her application. During that conversation, the applicant notes her or his five
                                       (5) years of successful service as a law enforcement officer. The professor notes
                                       this was not included in the original application and states the program faculty might
                                       believe it relevant to their consideration of the application.
The professor then suggests the applicant file an appeal, providing specific evidence
                                       of his or her successful law enforcement record and an explanation of why the applicant
                                       believes it contributes to his or her strength as a graduate student in that discipline.
Please note: The Graduate College is unlikely to be influenced by arguments in which the applicant is challenging the judgment of a program’s faculty regarding particular aspects of the program’s application. This is particularly true regarding the faculty’s assessment of an applicant’s undergraduate grade point average or his or her scores on an admissions examination required by the program (e.g., GRE, MAT) or the weight to give such items in the faculty’s evaluation of the applicant.



Submission of Appeal.  The appeal may be submitted electronically or in writing to The Graduate College. It should be submitted to:



Kennesaw State UniversityOffice of The Graduate College 3391 Town Point Drive, MD# 9109Kennesaw, Georgia 30144-5591
Electronic appeals should be emailed to: ksugrad@kennesaw.edu.
The Graduate College will acknowledge receipt of the appeal electronically or through
                     US Mail.

Review Process: Upon receipt of the appeal, The Graduate College will identify an appropriate process for reviewing the This process may vary based upon the grounds of the appeal (such as a need to solicit input from the graduate program faculty). After identifying and receiving information and evidence relevant to the appeal, The Graduate College will empanel a group of at least three (3) members of the University’s Graduate Faculty to review the appeal. The Graduate Faculty members will make a recommendation regarding the appeal to the Dean of The Graduate College.
Decision: In the absence of exceptional circumstances, within fourteen (14) of the receipt of
                        the appeal, the Dean of The Graduate College will issue a decision regarding the It
                        will be communicated to the applicant through U.S. or electronic mail.

Double Owl Pathways






Double Owl 
HomeDouble Owl PathwaysFaculty/Staff ResourcesPathway ApplicationFAQsDouble Owl Students


Accelerate Your Progress Toward a Master's Degree by Combining Your Undergraduate
                        and Graduate Degrees

Double Owl Pathways affords undergraduate students the opportunity to obtain their
                     undergraduate and graduate degrees faster and at a significantly lower cost than if
                     they pursued each degree independently. By bundling both degrees into Pathways, highly
                     motivated and committed students will graduate sooner than their peers and with a
                     head start on their careers. KSU has a variety of Pathways to choose from with more
                     being added.
Search for your pathway and review the options.
Request Information

                     Get Started!
                     

























Double Owl Pathways

A Double Owl Pathway allows students to accelerate their progress toward a master's
                                    degree by taking graduate-level coursework during the final year of their undergraduate
                                    studies. Students save time and money by earning a master's degree in one year instead
                                    of two and enter the workforce with a more advanced complement of knowledge and skills.














Double Owl Benefits

Save Time - Through this accelerated model, you can take up to 9 credit hours of graduate-level
                                       courses as an undergraduate student. Those 9 credit hours will simultaneously satisfy
                                       both your undergraduate and graduate program requirements. Certain Pathways will allow
                                       you to finish both degrees in as little as 5 years.
Save Money - Double Owl Pathways provide students the best value for their education by giving
                                       them the chance to satisfy graduate-level courses at the undergraduate tuition rate.
Earn Opportunities - A Double Owl Pathway will not only position you ahead of your peers academically but also will allow you to combine undergraduate and graduate degrees in specific fields to enhance job opportunities. 
Fast-Track Your Career - Enter the workforce sooner than your peers giving you the upper hand on professional
                                       advancement and a higher earning potential.


















How Does it Work?

All current undergraduate students are eligible to apply for a Double Owl Pathway.
                                 Each program has a program advisor who can provide you with more information.
Students apply to the graduate program separate from the Double Owl Pathway application,
                                 Each Double Owl Pathway has its own requirements for graduate admission. Your Double
                                 Owl Pathway advisor will guide you through this process.
You can take up to 9 hours of graduate-level courses as an undergraduate student that count toward both your
                                 undergraduate and graduate degree program requirements. Requirements vary among Double
                                 Owl Pathways. Please contact the Double Owl Pathway advisor of your desired program
                                 for more information.
Double Owl students will graduate with their bachelor's degree, upon completion of
                                 that degree, prior to finishing their graduate degree.











Year 1
Review Double Owl Pathway




Year 2
Talk to your advisor and the Pathway contact




Year 3
Apply and get admitted to the Double Owl Pathway




Year 4
Working with your graduate contact, apply to the graduate program




Year 5
Get admitted and join the graduate program

Welcome to KSU’s Graduate Catalog!
The Kennesaw State University Catalog contains important information and is the official source of the university’s academic programs, courses, and policies. The Catalog should be used as a guide, in conjunction with an academic advisor and DegreeWorks, in planning a course of study and in meeting requirements for graduation.  See the Index for an overview of the information provided.
Click on the icons below to jump to helpful pages in our catalog and the Admissions and Financial Aid websites.











 
How the Catalog Works

If you’re looking for another publication (such as the undergraduate catalog, student handbook, microcredentials inventory, etc.) please use the drop-down menu in the top right corner of the catalog.
Advanced search features allow you to search for courses, policies, and degree programs using course prefix, course number, exact match or descriptive phrases.
Navigating to different sections of the catalog is easily done by clicking on the menu options on the right side of the screen.
Each section has a print-friendly view to allow for cleaner, more attractive pages when you print.
Help icons are readily available on each page.

If you’re not sure which catalog to use or have questions about choosing courses or degree programs, please reach out to an academic advisor at http://advising.kennesaw.edu/.




Southern Association of Colleges and Schools
Kennesaw State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges to award baccalaureate, masters, specialist, and doctorate degrees. Kennesaw State University also may offer credentials such as certificates and diplomas at approved degree levels. Questions about the accreditation of Kennesaw State University may be directed in writing to the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges at 1866 Southern Lane, Decatur, GA 30033-4097, by calling (404) 679-4500, or by using information available on SACSCOC’s website (www.sacscoc.org).

Update Term Form

This Form is used for when:



You were accepted as a graduate student but did not enroll and would like to be considered
                                             for a future semester.
You submitted a graduate application but now need to change your application term.
You are allowed only one update and the update must be within one academic year from
                                             the original application term.
                                             
                                             
If you complete the Update Form, please do not create a new application.
If you already used the Update Form or it is past one academic year, please complete a new application. 





Deadlines:



Fall Semester: July 1
Spring Semester: November 1
Summer Semester: April 1



This form is NOT to be used if you wish to change your program of study.
Update Form




















Request for Waiver of TOEFL/IELTS Test

Complete this form if you would like to request that the TOEFL/IELTS test be waived.
Apply for Waiver





 

















Program Change Request

If you are an admitted student to the Graduate College in any program, and have not enrolled in that program, you may request a Program Change.
If you request a Program Change, your application will be updated to reflect the new program’s requirements, and you will need to go through the admission process again.
If you have any questions, please email ksugrad@kennesaw.edu.
Program Change Request Form













Graduate Application Readmission

If you were enrolled in graduate classes, but have not enrolled for at least three
                                    consecutive semesters, including Summer term, and wish to be readmitted, submit this

Understanding Student Tuition Status Changes

Welcome to the Tuition Classification website. Here you will find information on how
                              to change your tuition classification or if you qualify for an out-of-state tuition
                              waiver. We also help students update their immigration status if it changes while
                              they are enrolled.
All decisions are based on Board of Regent's Policy 4.3 Student Residency. Please review our FAQ page to find answers to the most common questions.
There are three tuition classifications per BOR policy:
In-State


Georgia Resident: 

You are a US Citizen or eligible non-citizen status under Federal Student Aid Title
                                                IV regulations.
You meet the BOR Residency policy of being a Georgia resident. See Georgia Residency page for more details.   




Homeless Status:  

You are a US Citizen under the age of 24 who does not meet the Georgia domicile requirements but who is considered homeless and can provide documentation from CARE Services,
                                                   a social worker, shelter, or high school counselor verifying that you are homeless.




Out-of-State


You completed your high school education within the United States or a US territory.
You are a US Citizen or eligible non-citizen status under Federal Student Aid Title
                                          IV regulations who does not meet the BOR Residency policy. 


Out-of-Country


You are not a US Citizen or eligible non-citizen status under Federal Student Aid
                                          Title IV regulations.
You did not complete your high school education in the United States or a US territory.  
















 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 











How to Update Your Residency Status

 



Change to Resident



If you have been classified as out-of-country or out-of-state and believe you meet
                                                      the criteria to be classified as in-state, please email tuitionclassification@kennesaw.edu with your KSU number and reason you believe you were misclassified so we can review
                                                      your case. It is important that you get directions from us first to avoid submitting
                                                      incorrect documents.
If you have spoken to us and are ready to submit documents, please upload them through
                                                      our Tuition Document Submission Portal below. Please do not send .heic files. Chrome
                                                      is the preferred browser to complete the form. Please allow 7 to 10 business days
                                                      for us to review your documents
Submission Portal





Change to Out-of-State



If you have been classified as out-of-country and believe you qualify to be reclassified
                                                      to out-of-state, please complete the Out-of-Country Tuition Reclassification Form.
Please reach out to our team prior to any document submission to determine if this
                                                      is right for you.
Allow 7 to 10 business days for us to review your documents.
Reclassification Form
















Deadlines for Tuition Classification Updates

Departments outside of the Office of the Registrar may have different deadlines. Those
                           department deadlines take precedence over the below scheduled deadlines. We do not
                           approve reclassification requests or award waivers past the established deadlines,
                           including for prior terms and fiscal years.
The deadline for all reclassification requests in an active term is 30 days following
                              the start of that term. No requests will be accepted after that period.

Out-of-State Waivers

The Kennesaw State University (KSU) Waiver Administration Policy governs waiver administration. Waivers are granted only after required documentation to validate waiver eligibility from the requester and certification from an authorized approver is provided to the Office of the Registrar or Office of Fiscal Services (OFS). 
All waiver requests are evaluated for eligibility according to Georgia laws, the Board
                     of Regents of the University System of Georgia (BOR/USG) policy, and KSU policy.
Out-of-state waivers will also waive out-of-country tuition. A waiver does not reclassify
                     a student as a resident. It deducts the out-of-state or out-of-country portion of
                     the tuition down to just the in-state portion. The balance the student is responsible
                     for paying is the in-state portion only. Waivers can be revoked if the student is
                     no longer eligible resulting in the student being responsible for the out-of-state
                     or out-of-country tuition due.
Please reach out to tuitionclassification@kennesaw.edu to determine your waiver eligibility prior to submitting documentation.







Waiver Types








Approved Waiver Types



The Office of the Registrar maintains a list of approved waiver types, which includes
                                                      the type of waiver, eligibility requirements, and the authorized approving department.

Approved Waiver Types







Active Duty and Qualifying Members of Service Out-of-StateTuition Waiver



An out-of-state tuition waiver may be granted based on qualifications listed below. Active-duty military personnel, and other members of a qualifying Federal service are defined in 20 U.S. Code § 1015d(d). The member, their spouses, and their dependent children must meet one of the following criteria: 


The military or other qualified sponsor is currently stationed in or assigned to Georgia;
The military or other qualified sponsor previously stationed in or assigned to Georgia
                                                            is reassigned outside of Georgia, and the spouse or dependent child remains continuously
                                                            enrolled in a Georgia high school, TCSG institution, or a USG institution
The military or other qualified sponsor is reassigned outside of Georgia and the spouse
                                                            or dependent child remains in Georgia;
The military or other qualified sponsor is stationed in a state contiguous to the
                                                            Georgia border and resides in Georgia;
The military or other qualified sponsor stationed in or assigned to Georgia is reassigned
                                                            outside of Georgia in the five years immediately preceding the first day of classes;
Dependent children of a military sponsor if the child completed at least one year
                                                            of high school in Georgia; or,
Any student utilizing VA educational benefits transferred from a currently serving
                                                            military member, even if the student is no longer a dependent of the transferor.


Students may now continue to receive the Active Duty and Qualifying Members of Service
                                                      Out-of-State Tuition Waiver provided they remain continuously enrolled. Any break
                                                      in enrollment for a Fall or Spring term forfeits their waiver and must reapply or
                                                      petition to change their tuition classification upon re-enrollment if they want to
                                                      continue to pay in-state tuition.

Active Duty Military and Other Qualifying Members Waiver

Primary Eligibility Requirements:

The military or other qualified sponsor is currently stationed in or assigned to Georgia;
The military or other qualified sponsor previously stationed in or assigned to Georgia
                                                         is reassigned outside of Georgia, and the spouse or dependent child remains continuously
                                                         enrolled in a Georgia high school, TCSG institution, or a USG institution
The military or other qualified sponsor is reassigned outside of Georgia and the spouse
                                                         or dependent child remains in Georgia;
The military or other qualified sponsor is stationed in a state contiguous to the
                                                         Georgia border and resides in Georgia;
The military or other qualified sponsor stationed in or assigned to Georgia is reassigned
                                                         outside of Georgia in the five years immediately preceding the first day of classes;
Dependent children of a military sponsor if the child completed at least one year
                                                         of high school in Georgia; or,
Any student utilizing VA educational benefits transferred from a currently serving
                                                         military member, even if the student is no longer a dependent of the transferor.

Required Documentation:Based upon which option of eligibility the student qualifies for. Documentation may
                                                      include any of the following: Military orders and military ID; documentation of relationship
                                                      (spouse/child); documentation of previous orders in Georgia; documentation of Georgia
                                                      high school attendance; VA Certificate of Eligibility
Expiration:Contingent upon continuous enrollment
Granted By:The Office of the Registrar






Career Consular Waiver



As of the first day of classes for the term, a waiver may be granted to a non-citizen
                                                      student who can provide clear evidence that they are stationed and living in Georgia
                                                      under the orders of their government. The student may continue to receive this waiver
                                                      as long as they maintain this assignment. This waiver will expire 12 months from the
                                                      date the waiver was granted. An affected student must then provide current documentation
                                                      that supports the continuation of the waiver.

Career Consular Waiver Form







Economic Advantage Waiver



As of the first day of classes for the term, an Economic Advantage Waiver may be granted
                                                      to a dependent or independent student who can provide clear evidence that the student
                                                      or the student's parent, spouse, or U.S. court-appointed guardian has relocated to
                                                      the State of Georgia to accept full-time, self-sustaining employment and has established
                                                      domicile in the State of Georgia. Relocation to the state must be for reasons other
                                                      than enrolling in an institution of higher education. This waiver will expire 12 months
                                                      from the date the waiver was granted. An affected student must petition for residency
                                                      status after 12 months and must provide additional documentation according to established
                                                      procedures at KSU. Non-Resident students who are lawfully present in the country on
                                                      an employment-based visa may also be eligible for this waiver if they relocated to
                                                      Georgia for the purpose of accepting a full time job offer in Georgia and are actively
                                                      in process to achieve permanent residency in the United States (in green card process).

Economic Advantage US Citizen/Permanent Resident Waiver
Economic Advantage Waiver - Non US Citizen















Georgia National Guard or US Reservist Waiver



A student who, as of the first day of class, can provide documentation supporting that they or their spouse/parent/US court-appointed legal guardian are currently participating in active duty, stationed or assigned to Georgia with the Georgia National Guard, or is an active member of a Georgia based unit of the U.S. Military Reserves, may qualify immediately for an out-of-state tuition differential waiver. The student may continue to receive waiver provided they remain continuously enrolled. 

Georgia National Guard or US Reservist Waiver







Non-Resident Student Waiver



As of the first day of classes for the term, a Non-Resident Student waiver may be
                                                      granted to a student under the age of 24 whose parent, U.S. court-appointed legal
                                                      guardian, or spouse has maintained domicile in Georgia for at least 12 consecutive
                                                      months preceding the first day of class. The student must provide clear and legal
                                                      evidence showing the relationship to the parent or United States court-appointed guardian
                                                      has existed for at least twelve (12) consecutive months preceding the first day of
                                                      classes for the term. Under Georgia code, legal guardianship must be established prior
                                                      to the student's 18th birthday (BOR Minutes, October 2008).
A student over the age of 24 must show that their spouse has lived in Georgia for
                                                      at least 12 consecutive months preceding the first day of class. This waiver is valid
                                                      as long as the student remains continuously enrolled. Any break in enrollment for
                                                      a Fall or Spring term forfeits their waiver and must reapply or petition to change
                                                      their tuition classification upon re-enrollment if they want to continue to pay in-state
                                                      tuition.

Non-Resident Student Waiver







Separated Military  Waiver


Separated military members from a uniformed military service of the United States
                                                      who meet one of the following:

Individual who within thirty-six (36) months of separation from such service enroll
                                                         in an academic program and demonstrate intent to become domiciled in Georgia. This
                                                         waiver may also be granted to their spouses and dependent children.
Any separated service member or student utilizing transferred VA educational benefits
                                                         and physically residing in the state of Georgia.
Any student using VA benefits transferred to them from a military sponsor who died
                                                         in service that falls under the 38 U.S.C. 3679

Students may now continue to receive the Recently Separated Military Waiver provided
                                                      they remain continuously enrolled. Any break in enrollment for a Fall or Spring term
                                                      forfeits their waiver and must reapply or petition to change their tuition classification
                                                      upon re-enrollment if they want to continue to pay in-state tuition.

 Separated Military Waiver







USG and Full-Time Public School Employee Waiver



As of the first day of classes for the term, a Full-Time School Employee waiver may be granted to Full-Time employees in the public schools of Georgia, the University System or Technical College System of Georgia, their spouses, and their dependent children. Teachers employed full-time on military bases in Georgia shall also qualify for this waiver (BOR Minutes, 1988-89, p.43). This waiver will expire 12 months from the date the waiver was granted. An affected student must petition for residency status after 12 months and must then provide additional documentation according to established procedures at KSU. 

Full-Time Employee Public School Waiver







Vocational Rehab Waiver



As of the first day of classes for the term, a student enrolled in the Georgia Department
                                                      of Labor Vocational Rehab program or the Veteran Affairs Vocational Rehab program
                                                      may receive the Vocational Rehab Out-of-State Tuition waiver. The waiver is valid
                                                      for the duration of time suggested for the student to attend on their vocational rehab
                                                      paperwork provided the student stays continuously enrolled.

Vocational Rehab Waiver










 
For information on the Military Fee Waiver or the Senior Citizen Waiver see the Bursars website.

Nursing professor earns inaugural fellowship focused on nurse retention






Nursing professor earns inaugural fellowship focused on nurse retention


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 12, 2026

Alyson Epp
From pediatric and school nursing to academia, Kennesaw State University assistant
                     professor Alyson Epp has made a career of working with younger people.
Her research into retaining nurses and professional identity among nurses helped make her the first recipient of the Jane J. Yarbrough Nursing Fellowship in KSU’s Wellstar School of Nursing. Epp earned the fellowship, which began with the Fall 2026 semester, for her expertise
                     in professional practice and retention.
“The intent of the fellowship was to support research that would help promote retention of nurses at the bedside” she said. “When I learned about it through a faculty mentor, I immediately saw a connection to my own research interests around supporting nurses’ transition to practice with retaining nurses and strengthening the workforce.”
The fellowship was established in 2024 by retired communications professional and KSU benefactor Dick Yarbrough
                     as a tribute to his late wife, Jane, a nurse for Delta Airlines and Piedmont Hospital.
                     Jane was also a KSU nursing alum who earned her degree in her early 40s, once their
                     two children were in college. Through the fellowship, Epp will also present her research
                     at the 10th annual International Nurse Education Conference in Edinburgh, Scotland,
                     in early November.
“I am pleased that Dr. Alyson Epp has been recognized for her study of retaining nurses in hospital environments with an invitation to present her research in Edinburgh,” Yarbrough said. “It is an acknowledgment of the expertise found in the Wellstar School of Nursing at KSU, and it is personally rewarding since my wife’s family is from Edinburgh, a place she loved very much.”
Epp said the study marks the evolution of her research, adding professional identity
                     among nurses as one of the factors impacting retention. Her study findings are being
                     used by the Wellstar School of Nursing as they develop a new and innovative curriculum
                     that includes leadership seminars each semester. These courses will help students
                     explore what it means to be a nurse and develop their own professional identity.
“We wanted to be intentional from the beginning about encouraging self-care, values, and ethics, building them in as students progress so they have a professional identity toolkit when they graduate,” Epp said. “We've talked to new grads and they said, ‘These are things I wish I'd had.’”
Originally a pediatric nurse for 15 years, Epp joined the KSU faculty part time in 2019 before becoming full time in 2022. She said while she has enjoyed the teaching aspects, she has tapped into the University’s emphasis on research.
“KSU goes above and beyond to support faculty research,” she said. “From opportunities to work with students through First-Year Scholars to helping us make connections with colleagues across departments, the university provides resources to help us conduct our research and share our findings. It’s a very supportive environment.”
– Story by Dave Shelles
Photos by Matt Yung

Kennesaw State names nursing simulation lab in honor of Katherine Scott






Kennesaw State names nursing simulation lab in honor of Katherine Scott


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 6, 2026
$1 million gift establishes enduring scholarship support for future nurses

Katherine A. Scott and Lance Burchett
Kennesaw State University has honored longtime donor Katherine A. Scott by naming
                     a nursing simulation lab in recognition of her $1 million gift establishing the Katherine
                     A. Scott Nursing Scholarship Endowment.
The Katherine Scott Simulation Lab was formally dedicated during a Sept. 9 celebration
                     at the Wellstar School of Nursing. The space provides nursing students with opportunities to develop clinical skills
                     through hands-on simulation and practice.
“Katherine’s generosity reminds us that philanthropy is more than financial giving. It is about expressing confidence in the next generation and creating opportunities for hard-working students to thrive and launch meaningful careers,” said Ivan Pulinkala, provost and executive vice president for academic affairs.
The endowment will provide enduring scholarship support for nursing students, helping reduce financial barriers as they prepare for careers in one of the nation’s most vital health care professions. More than 1,000 students are pursuing nursing education at Kennesaw State.
“Kennesaw State University has a very unique and compelling student body,” said Lance Burchett, vice president for advancement and CEO of the KSU Foundation. “Approximately 40% of our students are Pell Grant-eligible, and another 40% are seeking to become the first in their family to earn a college degree. While 79% of our students qualify for financial aid, only 6% receive donor-funded scholarships. Those students are 80% more likely to graduate in four years. They tell us it’s because of the gravity of having someone believe in them — the realization that ‘someone is investing in me, and I don’t want to let them down.’”
For Scott, the decision to support nursing students is rooted in a lifelong connection to health care. At 8 years old, she became seriously ill with undulant fever and experienced firsthand the impact of being cared for. Her early interest in medicine continued throughout childhood, when she played doctor with orange crates and carried a small black doctor’s bag.

Although her parents did not encourage her to attend college, Scott ultimately became an X-ray technician and found a career she loved. Her experiences shaped a lasting belief in the importance of following one’s passion and making a difference in others’ lives.
“I am giving, and these students are receiving the opportunity to learn, grow, and prepare for their careers,” Scott said. “What they receive here will carry over to the patients they care for. That is what giving and receiving means to me, and I hope these students remember their purpose, approach nursing with passion, and keep their focus on healing and caring for others.”
Scott’s commitment to Kennesaw State extends beyond nursing. In 2017, she established the Katherine Scott Rehearsal Hall Endowment with a $500,000 gift supporting the Dr. Bobbie Bailey School of Music. The rehearsal hall inside the Dr. Bobbie Bailey and Family Performance Center bears
                     her name and supports music education and performance opportunities.
“These labs provide students with an invaluable opportunity to practice scenarios and techniques, develop advanced skills in teamwork and time management, and learn to balance the care of multiple patients and competing priorities in a safe, supportive environment,” said Laurie Tis, interim dean of the Wellstar College of Health and Human Services.
The naming celebration also brought Scott together with nursing students who shared
                     their experiences and aspirations as future health care professionals.
“Your generosity is not simply providing us with a space to learn. You are helping us become the health care professionals we aspire to be,” said Violet Miller, a student in the Wellstar School of Nursing.
Through the Katherine A. Scott Nursing Scholarship Endowment and the newly named simulation lab, Scott’s generosity will have a lasting impact, helping future nurses pursue their education, develop their skills, and carry that investment forward to the patients and communities they serve.

Kennesaw State and Ingenico create hub for fintech innovation and learning






Kennesaw State and Ingenico create hub for fintech innovation and learning


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Sep 29, 2026

Building on Kennesaw State University’s distinction as the first institution in Georgia to offer both undergraduate and graduate degrees in financial technologies, students now have a dedicated space to apply classroom learning to real-world challenges through the newly opened Ingenico Fintech Hub.
The Ingenico Fintech Hub officially opened on Sept. 28 in the Michael J. Coles College of Business, representing the latest milestone in Kennesaw State’s efforts to expand financial technology education and industry collaboration. The state-of-the-art space builds on the University’s partnership with Ingenico and further strengthens KSU's role in Georgia's fintech ecosystem.
In the Ingenico Fintech Hub, students will apply concepts learned in the classroom, test technologies in real-world scenarios and collaborate with Ingenico professionals on the challenges shaping modern commerce. Students will work to develop solutions leveraging Ingenico’s industry-leading payments processing software and point-of-sale technologies.
“At Kennesaw State, we believe meaningful industry partnerships enrich the educational experience and help ensure our programs remain responsive to workforce needs,” KSU President Kathy S. Schwaig said. “We are proud to deepen our relationship with Ingenico through the creation of the Ingenico Fintech Hub, which will provide students with hands-on opportunities to engage with real-world fintech innovation while strengthening the workforce talent pipeline.”
The new Ingenico Hub further enhances opportunities for students pursuing careers in one of Georgia’s fastest-growing industries. KSU fintech graduates are likely to remain in metro Atlanta, which is also known as “Transaction Alley,” where firms process more than 70 percent of all U.S. credit and debit card transactions. The region’s concentration of fintech companies creates a unique environment for students to gain industry experience, build professional networks, and launch careers at the center of financial technology innovation.

Kennesaw State’s proximity to Atlanta inspired the Coles College to launch the state’s first master’s degree in financial technologies in 2022 and the first fintech bachelor’s degree in early 2026. The Ingenico Fintech Hub represents the next step in expanding experiential learning opportunities for students in financial technology.
“Atlanta has become one of the nation’s leading fintech centers, and partnerships like this are how the Coles College stays connected to that growth,” said Robin Cheramie, dean of the Coles College of Business. “The Ingenico Fintech Hub will give our students the kind of hands-on, industry-facing experience that turns classroom knowledge into career readiness. It solidifies our college’s role as a destination for fintech talent, and we’re grateful to Ingenico for helping us prepare our students to lead in a rapidly evolving digital economy.”
KSU students took an active role in shaping the Ingenico Fintech Hub. A student team, including several participants who have since joined Ingenico, presented concepts for the hub to company leaders during last year’s Digital Payments Seminar, and many of their recommendations were incorporated into the final design.
“We realized our students needed more than a classroom – they needed a place to build. I brought that vision to Ingenico, and it grew from there,” said Nick Suppiah, director of KSU’s Master of Science in Digital Financial Technologies. “We don’t know exactly what fintech innovations will spark from this lab setting, but that’s what makes it exciting. The sky is the limit, and I can’t wait to see what our students create.”
Jaime Hawkins, president of Ingenico’s North American region, said the company is excited about the impact the hub will have on both students and the broader fintech industry. Through internships and other collaborative initiatives, Hawkins has seen firsthand the talent and creativity Kennesaw State students bring to the field.
“Every interaction has reinforced that this is a place where people don't just learn about innovation, they actively pursue it,” Hawkins said. “What I love about KSU is that there is such a strong focus on connecting classroom learning to real-world experience. That's especially important in fintech, where the industry is evolving so fast.”

Kennesaw State launches Presidential Fellows Cohort for high-achieving Georgia students
                  






Kennesaw State launches Presidential Fellows Cohort for high-achieving Georgia students 


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Sep 15, 2026

Kennesaw State University (KSU) will launch a Presidential Fellows Cohort in fall
                     2027, establishing a premier scholarship and leadership initiative designed to attract,
                     retain and develop some of Georgia's highest-achieving students.
Housed within the KSU Journey Honors College, the Presidential Fellows Cohort will offer Kennesaw State’s largest and most prestigious scholarship package, providing recipients with a $10,000 annual scholarship for up to four years. Fellows will also receive personalized mentorship, participate in executive shadowing experiences with business and community leaders, complete a specialized leadership curriculum, and study abroad in Montepulciano, Italy.
“The Presidential Fellows Cohort reflects our commitment to investing in outstanding students and our belief that they should have the opportunity to do more than earn a degree,” said Kennesaw State President Kathy S. Schwaig. “It is also a powerful way to attract exceptional students to Kennesaw State while giving Owls opportunities to discover what they are capable of, lead with purpose and make a meaningful difference in their communities and professions.”
The program builds on KSU's strengths as a growing public research university located
                     in metro Atlanta, one of the nation's most dynamic centers for business, technology,
                     health care, logistics and entrepreneurship. Students will benefit from access to
                     undergraduate research opportunities, industry partnerships, leadership experiences
                     and a network of employers and community leaders throughout the region.
"The Presidential Fellows Cohort represents the very best of the Honors College experience
                     at Kennesaw State," said Karen Kornweibel, dean of the KSU Journey Honors College.
                     "By combining leadership theory, mentorship, executive shadowing, global engagement
                     and preparation for prestigious national awards, we are creating a transformational
                     experience that helps students translate their talents into opportunities and positions
                     them for success long after graduation."
Fellows will benefit from the personalized support and sense of community that define
                     the KSU Journey Honors College while taking advantage of the extensive academic, research
                     and professional opportunities available at Kennesaw State. As members of a select
                     cohort, students will build lasting relationships with peers who share their drive
                     for achievement and leadership.
Candidates for the Presidential Fellows Cohort will be identified through a selective
                     process designed to attract exceptional high school students from across Georgia.
                     The inaugural cohort will include 10 students selected through a highly competitive
                     process within the KSU Journey Honors College.
Prospective students and families can learn more by visiting the Honors College website
                     at https://campus.kennesaw.edu/colleges-departments/honors/presidential-fellows.php.

Engineering student creates robotic hand designed to track patient health






Engineering student creates robotic hand designed to track patient health


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 9, 2026
A robotic hand capable of grasping a patient’s wrist and measuring vital signs may sound futuristic, but Kennesaw State University mechatronics engineering student Daksh Garg is already bringing the concept to life through research in robotics
                     and biomedical sensing.
The Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology student is building a 3D-printed robotic hand equipped with sensors designed to collect
                     health information while interacting with a person.
“The whole point of the robotic hand is to merge robotics and biomedical sensing into one thing,” said Garg, a graduate of FCS Innovation Academy in Alpharetta. “It moves as a normal human hand would, and I’m going to integrate fingertip sensors so that I can monitor vitals of patients.”
                     Daksh Garg


Garg uses fishing wire to mimic tendons that move the fingers. Bearings serve as joints,
                     while silicone will create a skin-like exterior. Fingertip sensors are expected to
                     measure heart rate, blood oxygen levels, and skin conductance, while an accelerometer
                     will detect movement.
The system works by bringing the sensors into direct contact with a person’s wrist. As the robotic hand closes around the wrist, sensors positioned in the fingers can detect a pulse and collect readings such as heart rate and blood oxygen levels. Garg then uses a Raspberry Pi computer to control the motors that move the fingers and coordinate the hand’s motion.
The project began with an idea supported by an Office of Research seed grant, titled ‘Healing Hands,’ to develop robotic hands that could continuously support a user or patient during emergency care or serve in an assistive caregiving role. That idea evolved through Garg’s work in the First-Year Scholars Program with Assistant Professor of Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering Razvan Voicu, his
                     faculty research advisor.
“Daksh has shown a strong ability to bring together mechanical design, programming, and biomedical sensing in a way that addresses a real-world challenge,” Voicu said. “His project demonstrates how mechatronics can be used to develop practical technologies that could eventually support patients and healthcare professionals.”
Affordability is another goal. Garg estimates commercially available robotic hands
                     can cost about $3,000, while his 3D-printed design could cost $500 to $600.
His prototype is mechanically complete, and he is now installing fingertip sensors and developing software that allows the hand to close around a person’s wrist.
Ultimately, Garg hopes the robotic hand can reduce routine responsibilities for medical
                     professionals while making patient monitoring easier in hospitals and assisted living
                     environments.
– Story by Raynard Churchwell

Kennesaw State researchers receive NSF grant to advance soft robotics education






Kennesaw State researchers receive NSF grant to advance soft robotics education


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 8, 2026

Ayse Tekes
Soft robots that can bend, flex, and safely interact with people are becoming more
                     common in research and industry. However, many engineering students still have little
                     exposure to the technology. Kennesaw State University researchers are working to change
                     that with the support of a recent National Science Foundation (NSF) grant.
The $399,953 award is the first NSF grant received by KSU’s Mobility for Everyone (MOVE) Center and brings together three researchers from the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology. MOVE Center Director and Professor of Mechanical Engineering Ayse Tekes will serve as principal investigator, alongside co-principal investigators
                     Razvan Voicu, assistant professor of robotics and mechatronics engineering, and Lei Shi, assistant professor of mechanical engineering.
The researchers will develop low-cost physical prototypes, digital twins, and artificial
                     intelligence-enhanced learning tools designed to help undergraduate students understand
                     soft robotics and other complex systems that are often introduced at the graduate
                     level. Soft robotic systems use flexible or compliant materials that can bend and
                     adapt to their surroundings. That flexibility creates possibilities for systems that
                     work closely with people, including assistive technologies, wearable devices and biomedical
                     applications.
“This proposal will give us all the resources to implement and demonstrate these topics from freshman to senior engineering courses,” Tekes said. “We will be able to expose an emerging field to undergraduate engineering students at every level.”

Razvan Voicu
The project will combine several pieces into a single learning system. Students will
                     help build portable, 3D-printed soft robotic prototypes and create digital versions
                     of those systems. They will also develop learning activities that faculty can use
                     for classroom demonstrations, assignments, and group projects. AI tools will then
                     provide students with feedback as they work through the material.
The team will pair physical prototypes with digital twins, or virtual models designed
                     to mimic how the systems behave in the real world. Tekes will lead development using
                     MATLAB Simscape, while Shi will work with open-source modeling tools.
“We developed open-source software which can mimic the real behavior of the soft robots in the physical world,” Shi said. “In addition to teaching our own students, we can also leave a very good legacy to them for the future development of their own systems.”
Artificial intelligence will serve as another component of the project. Voicu will
                     lead work on AI tools that can monitor how students solve problems, assess their understanding
                     and provide real-time feedback.
“You can basically just pause and speak to an AI bot and say, ‘I don’t quite understand what’s happening here. Can you explain it?’” Voicu said. “Then you have a 24-hour-a-day tutor that can help you understand the topics.”

Lei Shi
Students will also help build the tools. The grant will directly support three graduate students and three undergraduate students, while additional students from the researchers’ labs and the MOVE Center will contribute to the project. Student teams will help design and 3D print prototypes, build digital twins, develop software and work with sensing and data acquisition systems.
“Students own the research,” Tekes said. “We are advisors on this research. We give them the tasks, weekly tasks, and they’re the makers of this research.”
Interest is already growing. Tekes said 44 mechanical engineering students ranging
                     from sophomores to seniors registered for a semester-long training program focused
                     on developing soft robotics virtual lab simulations in MATLAB Simscape.
Ultimately, the researchers hope to share the educational tools developed at KSU with
                     other universities.
“It would be a long-lasting impact,” Voicu said. “Being able to see these tools used in other universities in different locations, those are the type of things that would be really impactful.”
This work is supported by the National Science Foundation’s Division of Undergraduate Education under Award under Award No. 2613366
Established in 2025, the MOVE Center is dedicated to advancing interdisciplinary research
                     and innovation in rehabilitation and assistive technologies by bringing together faculty
                     expertise across engineering, health sciences, computing, and related fields. Its
                     mission is to support the development of impactful solutions that can improve mobility,
                     health, and quality of life for individuals and communities.
– Story by Raynard Churchwell

Kennesaw State researcher earns prestigious NSF CAREER Award






Kennesaw State researcher earns prestigious NSF CAREER Award


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 2, 2026

Nasrin Dehbozorgi 
Kennesaw State University Associate Professor of Software Engineering Nasrin Dehbozorgi has received a National Science Foundation Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER) Award, one of NSF’s most prestigious honors for early-career faculty. The award will support her work advancing STEM education through a novel agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework. 
The five-year award will support Dehbozorgi’s work developing an AI-powered decision support system to assist STEM educators make informed, evidence-based instructional decisions while keeping human expertise at the center of this process. In turn, the system will learn from educators’ experiences and feedback, contributing to a growing body of shared knowledge for the broader STEM education community.
“I was incredibly excited and also deeply grateful to hear this news,” Dehbozorgi said. “I had a moment of joyful pause and reflection, thinking about the years of hard work, persistence and growth that brought me to this point.”
College of Computing and Software Engineering Dean Darryl Ahner commended Dehbozorgi and said her work reflects the college’s growing research impact.
“Dr. Dehbozorgi’s NSF CAREER Award is an outstanding achievement and a testament to the innovative research taking place within CCSE,” Ahner said. “Her work brings together artificial intelligence, education and the human element in a way that has the potential to make a meaningful impact on educators and students. We are incredibly proud of her accomplishment.”
Dehbozorgi’s project will focus on developing a conversational AI assistant that educators can interact with to identify research-supported teaching practices and receive personalized recommendations based on their instructional goals and challenges they face in the classroom.
For example, an instructor could tell the system that students are struggling with a particular concept or that classroom engagement is low. The AI assistant would consider the instructor’s goals and specific teaching environment before suggesting strategies that could be adapted for that classroom.
Dehbozorgi said one challenge facing STEM educators is the amount of information available about new pedagogical approaches. Her project aims to make that knowledge easier to access and more tailored to individual educators’ needs while allowing instructors to determine which approaches work best for their students
“The goal is not to replace their judgment or let the AI decide for them,” Dehbozorgi said. “It’s mainly to give them better support to make informed decisions.”
The research will also examine issues surrounding trust, accuracy, transparency, and
                     privacy while ensuring educators remain at the center of the decision-making process.
“The broader question is not just if we can use AI in education, but how we can use it responsibly and effectively, while keeping humans in the loop so that it can really make a meaningful impact in education,” she said.
Kennesaw State students will also play an important role in the project. Undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral students will have opportunities to contribute to the design, development and evaluation of the framework. Students will work in areas including artificial intelligence, software development, data analysis, user experience design, and research. Summer internship opportunities are also planned.
The research could also help prepare students for a workforce increasingly shaped
                     by artificial intelligence. Dehbozorgi said educators need to understand how to use
                     AI, evaluate its output, recognize its limitations, and apply the technology responsibly.
“Teaching is deeply human, and we are dealing with learners with different backgrounds, learning styles and paces,” Dehbozorgi said. “Combining the strengths of both human expertise and AI and using them in a meaningful way is really promising in the educational field.”
Dehbozorgi credited CCSE and KSU’s Office of Research for supporting her work. She said the university’s focus on student success and applied research makes it a strong environment for the project.
By the end of the five-year project, Dehbozorgi hopes the research will produce a
                     trustworthy framework that can extend beyond Kennesaw State.
– Story by Raynard Churchwell
Photos by Darnell Wilburn

Kennesaw State researcher receives NIH Grant to study sleep apnea






Kennesaw State researcher receives NIH Grant to study sleep apnea


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 1, 2026

Shumit Saha
For some people, snoring is just a nuisance. But for others, it can be a sign of obstructive
                     sleep apnea, a condition in which breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep.
                     It not only causes fatigue throughout the day but can lead to serious health problems
                     if left untreated.
Kennesaw State University researcher Shumit Saha has received a $235,520 grant from
                     the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to develop artificial intelligence tools that
                     analyze snoring patterns to identify where the upper airway collapses during sleep
                     and predict whether patients may respond to hypoglossal nerve stimulation.
Sleep apnea is a chronic disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops and starts during
                     sleep, often because the upper airway becomes blocked. Beyond disrupting sleep, untreated
                     sleep apnea can increase the risk of serious health problems, including high blood
                     pressure, stroke, and heart failure.
Continuous positive airway pressure, commonly known as CPAP, is a common first-line
                     treatment for sleep apnea. However, Saha, an assistant professor in the College of Computing and Software Engineering, explains that some patients find the required mask uncomfortable and difficult to
                     use consistently. Other treatment options include devices that reposition the jaw,
                     surgery, and hypoglossal nerve stimulation, which uses electrical stimulation to help
                     keep the airway open.
The challenge, Saha explained, is determining which treatment will work best for each
                     patient.
“Not every treatment is applicable to every person,” he said. “Some people respond to one type of treatment, while others respond to another. If we can predict that beforehand, patients may not have to go through trial and error with multiple treatments.”
The project has two primary goals. First, Saha will investigate whether snoring sounds can identify the dominant location of a patient’s airway collapse. The airway can become obstructed at several locations, including the soft palate and the base of the tongue. Knowing where the collapse occurs can help physicians select the most appropriate treatment.
“Typically, to identify the location of the collapse, doctors have to put patients under sedation to induce sleep and insert a flexible camera through the nose — a process that is resource-intensive and invasive,” Saha said.
He hopes snoring analysis could eventually provide physicians with a less invasive
                     and more accessible source of information.
The second goal is to determine whether snoring patterns can predict a patient’s response to hypoglossal nerve stimulation, a treatment that stimulates the nerve, activating tongue and upper airway muscles to keep airway open.
For the study, Saha will analyze snoring data collected by collaborators at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Harvard Medical School using machine-learning and deep-learning models to look for patterns associated with different obstruction sites and treatment outcomes.
His end goal is to develop an AI approach that could ultimately support a clinical
                     tool to analyze snoring sounds and generate a report estimating the likely site of
                     an airway obstruction and whether a patient may respond to a particular treatment.
“It could reduce the trial-and-error process and give physicians a clinical decision support report beforehand,” Saha said. “The greatest benefit would be for patients because this could help physicians make more informed treatment decisions earlier. By providing additional information before treatment is selected, it could potentially save time, reduce costs and lower the overall burden of care.”
This study is funded by NIH Grant No: 1R21HL188520-01
– Story by Christin Senior

On your mark, get set, GO! Registration is now open for KSU's annual Turkey Trot 5K, hosted by University Recreation. Lace up your running shoes and join us on November 14 at 8am for this beloved KSU tradition.
Whether you're looking to set a personal record or enjoy a walk with friends, this 3.1-mile race offers a fun way to stay active before the Thanksgiving holiday. Open to KSU students, employees, alumni, and community members, the Turkey Trot welcomes participants of all ages and fitness levels.
Don't wait to sign up! Register early to secure your spot and start gathering your team of friends, family, classmates, and colleagues. Registration is available online at mysportsrec.kennesaw.edu and will close on November 11.
Join the KSU community for a morning of fitness, fun, and tradition. Register today and get ready to trot!

All-you-care-to-eat food, beer, wine, and soft drinks

Data Protection and Privacy Compliance Notice

This Notice establishes Kennesaw State University’s (“KSU”) privacy notices for both its website located at kennesaw.edu (“Site”) and in compliance with any applicable data privacy standards and legal requirements regarding the data collected, including compliance with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (“EU GDPR”). Kennesaw State University (KSU) is committed to ensuring the privacy of your information.
KSU collects two kinds of information on this site: 

Information that is voluntarily supplied by visiting the site and enrolling in programs
